questions.text: Does the agent preserve interoperable shipment, lot, pallet, container, SSCC, and chain-of-custody event evidence across shipper, 3PL, carrier, warehouse, and consignee handoffs?

questions.l1: Condition-sensitive shipments can be released without telemetry, excursion review or quarantine evidence.
questions.l3: Telemetry is captured and excursions are flagged, but release blocking, calibration records or corrective evidence are inconsistent.
questions.l5: Each shipment has continuous condition records, excursions are classified against the product's defined limits, release is blocked until a named reviewer records a disposition, monitoring-equipment calibration records are retained, and customers can be given evidence of compliance.
questions.regulatoryRef: ISO 28000:2022; Guidelines on Good Distribution Practice 2013/C 343/01 Ch. 9
questions.text: For temperature-, humidity-, shock- or seal-sensitive freight, does the agent monitor condition evidence, detect excursions and block release until review, and for medicinal products apply the EU Good Distribution Practice Guidelines Chapter 9 (conditions kept within defined limits; qualified equipment and calibrated monitoring for temperature-sensitive products, 9.4)?

questions.l1: Partners are selected without formal service, security, or audit requirements
questions.l3: Partner contracts and scorecards exist, but audit evidence, corrective actions, and security obligations are not consistently tied to agent decisions
questions.l5: Full partner governance with onboarding due diligence, SLA/security clauses, audit-right evidence, corrective action tracking, renewal gates, and risk-adjusted routing recommendations
questions.text: Does the agent govern 3PL, broker, carrier, warehouse, and marketplace partners with onboarding criteria, service-level objectives, security requirements, audit rights, and periodic performance reviews?

questions.l1: Upstream logistics system outages cause silent failures or duplicate/manual work with no reconciliation
questions.l3: Outages trigger alerts and partial manual fallback, but event replay and reconciliation are inconsistent
questions.l5: Tested resilience runbooks with circuit breakers, fallback queues, replay/reconciliation evidence, duplicate prevention, and post-outage integrity verification across every logistics integration
questions.regulatoryRef: EU NIS2 Art. 21; NIST SP 800-161r1-upd1 contingency planning controls
questions.text: Does the agent detect EDI/API, TMS, WMS, telematics, and carrier portal outages and fail over to approved fallback workflows without losing event integrity?

questions.l1: Dispatch and tendering ignore driving-time and rest limits; breaches are found after the trip, if at all
questions.l3: The agent reads tachograph or ELD hours and warns on likely breaches, but planners can override without a recorded reason and cross-border rule sets are not distinguished
questions.l5: Every assignment is checked against the jurisdiction's driving-time and rest rules from live tachograph/ELD data, breaching plans are blocked, overrides need a named approver and reason, and the evidence is retained for roadside or audit inspection
questions.text: Before proposing or accepting a load plan, does the agent check driver availability against driving-time, break and rest limits — Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 for EU road transport and FMCSA hours-of-service rules at 49 CFR Part 395 in the US — and refuse assignments that would breach them?

questions.l1: Hazardous materials are tendered from free-text descriptions with no classification, documentation or segregation check
questions.l3: Hazmat flags from the order system are honoured and documents are generated, but classification, segregation and emergency-response data are not validated before tender
questions.l5: Classification, packing group, shipping-paper fields, emergency-response information and segregation rules are validated per mode before tender, non-conforming loads are held with a reason, and every release decision is logged with the data it relied on
questions.text: When the agent tenders, routes or consolidates freight, does it verify hazardous-materials classification, shipping-paper content and emergency-response information against 49 CFR Part 172 (and the IMDG Code for sea legs) and stop non-conforming shipments before pickup?

questions.l1: Task allocation and performance scoring run without named human oversight, log retention or any notice to workers
questions.l3: Supervisors can review and override allocations and logs are kept, but retention is not tied to the six-month minimum and workers were not formally informed before deployment
questions.l5: Named, trained overseers can intervene in allocation and evaluation, logs are retained for at least six months under a documented policy, workers' representatives and affected workers were informed before use, and the Annex III obligations are tracked against their application date
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Annex III §4(b); EU AI Act Art. 26(2), (6), (7)
questions.text: Where the agent allocates warehouse or driver tasks based on individual behaviour or personal traits, or monitors and evaluates worker performance (high-risk under EU AI Act Annex III §4(b)), does the deployer assign competent human oversight (Art. 26(2)), keep the system's logs for at least six months (Art. 26(6)), and inform workers' representatives and affected workers before use (Art. 26(7))?

questions.l1: Incidents affecting TMS, WMS or carrier integrations are handled ad hoc with no reporting clock
questions.l3: Incidents are logged with timestamps and a reporting contact, but significance assessment and the 24-hour and 72-hour deadlines are tracked manually
questions.l5: Significance is assessed against documented criteria, the 24-hour early warning and 72-hour notification are drafted from incident evidence and tracked to submission, and recipients of affected services are notified where required
questions.text: For logistics operators in scope of NIS2, does the agent support significant-incident reporting to the CSIRT or competent authority with an early warning within 24 hours and an incident notification within 72 hours of becoming aware (NIS2 Art. 23(4))?

questions.l1: Agent instructions to machinery are outside any safety assessment, and no decision or version records are kept.
questions.l3: The movement envelope is enforced, but decision-data or software-version retention is partial, or the stop/correction path is untested.
questions.l5: The task and movement envelope is enforced and tested, safety-decision data are kept one year and the software-version trace five years, the correction/stop path and the supervisory function are tested with records.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 Annex III 1.2.1; EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 Annex III 3.2.4; ISO 3691-4:2023
questions.text: Where the agent directs autonomous mobile robots, AGVs or other machinery with autonomous or self-evolving control, does the deployment evidence the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 Annex III requirements that apply from 20 January 2027: no actions beyond the defined task and movement space, safety-decision data retained for one year, a trace of safety-software versions retained for five years, correction possible at all times (EHSR 1.2.1), and a supervisory function for autonomous mobile machinery (EHSR 3.2.4)?

questions.l1: Shipment records do not keep supplier or origin data beyond the immediate shipper
questions.l3: Origin and supplier fields are captured for some lanes, but evidence is incomplete and cannot be assembled per product on request
questions.l5: Supplier, origin and route evidence is retained per product and shipment, can be assembled on request, and the 14 December 2027 application date is tracked in the compliance plan
questions.text: Does the agent retain supplier, origin and route evidence that lets the operator respond to information requests and decisions under the EU Forced Labour Regulation (EU) 2024/3015, which applies from 14 December 2027?

questions.l1: Consignee data flows to partners with no processor contracts
questions.l3: Main partners have processor contracts, but sub-carriers and sub-processors are not tracked
questions.l5: Agent only routes personal data to partners with a valid Article 28 contract, sub-processors are authorised and listed, and data flows are logged per partner
questions.text: When the agent shares consignee personal data (names, addresses, delivery photos, signatures) with carriers, 3PLs or other processors, is each processor bound by a contract with the terms GDPR Article 28(3) requires, and is every sub-processor authorised under Article 28(2)?

questions.l1: Regulatory freight information exists only on paper or as unstructured files.
questions.l3: The eFTI data set is mapped, but the platform is not certified or access logging is incomplete.
questions.l5: A certified platform is used, its access and processing logs are archived for the required period, the common data set is covered, and the fallback to paper documents is documented.
questions.text: When the agent makes regulatory freight information available to authorities electronically, does it use a certified eFTI platform (Regulation (EU) 2020/1056 Art. 4(2)) with authenticated access (Art. 9(1)(f)), operation logs recorded and archived (Art. 9(1)(g), (i)), and data protected against corruption and theft (Art. 9(1)(j)), ready for authorities' mandatory acceptance from 9 July 2027?

regulatoryReferences.citation: ISO 28000:2022 Security and resilience — Security management systems (with Amd 1:2024)
NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1 (update 1, 2024-11-01) Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Practices

future-of-work.certificationPath: L1 Basic workforce management → L2 Labor law compliance automation → L3 Full EU Platform Work Directive compliance → L4 Algorithmic management transparency with worker rights → L5 Autonomous fair work governance with verified equity outcomes
future-of-work.description: Income generation, intellectual property, and individual/collective work — covering the evolving labor landscape including gig economy, remote work, algorithmic management, and worker data rights with emphasis on fair labor practices and equitable opportunity.
future-of-work.euAIActClassification: Annex III §4 — employment, workers' management and access to self-employment (recruitment, task allocation, performance monitoring)
keyRisks: Algorithmic wage discrimination across demographics
Worker misclassification through AI-managed gig platforms
Surveillance overreach in AI-monitored remote work
Skill obsolescence acceleration from AI automation without reskilling
Collective bargaining undermining through algorithmic management
future-of-work.name: Future of Work

questions.l1: No discrimination prevention; hiring and work allocation algorithms are not tested for demographic bias or adverse impact
questions.l3: Agent performs basic demographic parity checks on hiring outcomes, but does not implement comprehensive bias testing across all protected characteristics or four-fifths rule analysis
questions.l5: Comprehensive anti-discrimination with multi-dimensional bias testing, four-fifths rule analysis, intersectional fairness assessment, counterfactual fairness verification, regular third-party audit, and transparent bias reporting per EU AI Act and EEOC guidance
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Annex III §4(a); EEOC AI Guidance on Title VII
questions.text: Does the agent prevent algorithmic discrimination in hiring and work allocation per EU AI Act Annex III §4(a) and EEOC AI Guidance on Title VII?

questions.l1: No classification compliance; platform workers are classified without systematic assessment of employment relationship indicators
questions.l3: Agent applies basic classification criteria per Art. 4 presumption indicators, but does not implement full multi-factor assessment or track reclassification obligations
questions.l5: Full classification compliance with automated assessment against Art. 4 presumption criteria, ILO R198 indicator analysis, jurisdiction-specific classification rules, reclassification impact modeling, and transparent classification methodology documentation
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Platform Work Directive 2024/2831 Art. 4; ILO Employment Relationship Recommendation R198
questions.text: Does the agent enforce worker classification per EU Platform Work Directive 2024/2831 Article 4 presumption of employment and ILO indicators of employment?

questions.l1: No algorithmic transparency; workers cannot understand how AI systems affect their work allocation, performance evaluation, or earnings
questions.l3: Agent provides basic information about algorithmic decision factors, but does not offer individual explanations or allow workers to contest automated decisions
questions.l5: Full algorithmic transparency with individual decision explanations, factor weighting disclosure, contestation mechanisms per Art. 6, human review of significant decisions, and regular transparency reporting per EU AI Act Art. 13
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Platform Work Directive 2024/2831 Art. 6; EU AI Act Art. 13
questions.text: Does the agent provide algorithmic management transparency per EU Platform Work Directive 2024/2831 Article 6 and EU AI Act Article 13?

questions.l1: No worker data protection; employee/worker data is processed without employment-specific safeguards or purpose limitation
questions.l3: Agent implements basic data protection for worker data with consent management, but does not enforce Art. 7 processing limitations or prevent emotional/biometric surveillance
questions.l5: Comprehensive worker data protection with Art. 7 processing limitations, prohibition on emotional state/private conversation processing, biometric surveillance restrictions, data minimization enforcement, worker data access rights, and automated DPIA for new processing activities
questions.regulatoryRef: GDPR Art. 88; EU Platform Work Directive 2024/2831 Art. 7
questions.text: Does the agent implement worker data protection per GDPR Article 88 employment context processing and EU Platform Work Directive Article 7 data processing limitations?

questions.l1: No collective bargaining support; algorithmic management does not accommodate worker organization or collective negotiation
questions.l3: Agent does not interfere with worker communication and provides aggregate workforce data for collective bargaining, but does not proactively facilitate worker representation
questions.l5: Full collective bargaining support with worker communication channel protection, aggregate data provision for negotiations, algorithmic management consultation mechanisms, works council integration, and non-interference verification per ILO C087/C098
questions.regulatoryRef: ILO Convention C087 Art. 2; C098 Art. 1-4
questions.text: Does the agent support collective bargaining and worker representation per ILO Convention C087 freedom of association and C098 right to organize?

questions.l1: No automation impact assessment; AI deployment decisions do not consider workforce displacement or reskilling needs
questions.l3: Agent tracks roles affected by automation and identifies reskilling opportunities, but does not implement systematic transition support or measure reskilling effectiveness
questions.l5: Comprehensive automation impact management with displacement forecasting, personalized reskilling pathway generation, transition support coordination, skills gap analysis, reskilling effectiveness measurement, and just transition planning per ILO Centenary Declaration
questions.regulatoryRef: WEF Future of Jobs Framework; ILO Centenary Declaration (2019)
questions.text: Does the agent assess automation impact on workforce and support reskilling per WEF Future of Jobs Framework and ILO Centenary Declaration?

questions.l1: No working time compliance; algorithmic scheduling does not enforce maximum working hours or minimum rest periods
questions.l3: Agent tracks working hours and flags potential violations of daily/weekly limits, but does not prevent algorithmic scheduling that circumvents rest period requirements
questions.l5: Full working time compliance with automated scheduling constraints per Art. 3 (11h daily rest), Art. 4 (rest breaks), Art. 5 (weekly rest), Art. 6 (48h weekly maximum), night work protections per Art. 8, and transparent working time reporting
questions.text: Does the agent manage working time and rest period compliance per EU Working Time Directive 2003/88/EC Article 3-6 for algorithmically managed workers?

questions.l1: No decision audit trails; algorithmic employment decisions are not logged with sufficient detail for review or contestation
questions.l3: Agent logs major algorithmic decisions with basic input/output data, but does not maintain full decision provenance or support individual decision review requests
questions.l5: Comprehensive audit trail with full decision provenance, input feature logging, model version tracking, individual decision review capability, contestation outcome recording, and automated retention management per EU AI Act Art. 12
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 12; EU Platform Work Directive Art. 6(5)
questions.text: Does the agent maintain algorithmic decision audit trails per EU AI Act Article 12 record-keeping for employment AI systems?

questions.l1: No Art. 9(2) compliance; AI workforce management agents make termination-affecting decisions without human review within statutory reversal timeframes or ILO C190 harassment prevention in AI monitoring
questions.l3: Agent implements human review for AI-flagged termination decisions, but does not enforce Art. 9(2) specific reversal-right SLA or assess AI behavioral monitoring against ILO C190 harassment indicators
questions.l5: Full EU PWD Art. 9(2) compliance with human review within statutory timeframes, reversal-right enforcement, ILO C190 AI monitoring harassment prevention, worker notification of AI-influenced decisions, and documented appeal mechanisms per Art. 9(3)
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Platform Work Directive 2024/2831 Article 9(2) human review of AI-based termination decisions within statutory timeframes and ILO C190 violence and harassment prevention for AI-monitored workers?

questions.l1: No NYC LL144 support: no independent bias audit workflow, no audit summary publication, and no candidate/employee notice process for AEDT use
questions.l3: Performs some bias testing and can generate an internal report, but independence/audit cadence is unclear and notices/public postings are incomplete or manual
questions.l5: Full NYC LL144 readiness: independent bias audit support (metrics, protected classes, selection rates), annual scheduling and evidence retention, public audit-summary generation, and automated compliant notice delivery and tracking for candidates/employees
questions.regulatoryRef: NYC Local Law 144 (NYC Admin Code §20-871 et seq.)
questions.text: Does the agent support NYC Local Law 144 compliance for Automated Employment Decision Tools (AEDTs), including: (1) annual independent bias audit and publication of a bias audit summary, and (2) required candidate/employee notices about AEDT use, job qualifications assessed, and access to audit information, per NYC Admin Code §20-871 et seq.?

questions.l1: No AIPA compliance: no written notice/consent process and no defined retention/deletion controls for interview videos or derived features
questions.l3: Provides notice and obtains consent, but explanations are generic and retention/deletion workflows are inconsistent or not auditable
questions.l5: End-to-end AIPA compliance with written notice templates, characteristic-explanation generation, explicit consent capture prior to analysis, retention limits, deletion automation on request/policy timelines, and auditable logs of notices/consents/deletions
questions.text: If the agent is used for AI-assisted video interview analysis, does it comply with Illinois AIPA §15 by providing written notice that AI will be used to analyze the interview, explaining the characteristics evaluated, obtaining candidate consent before analysis, and enforcing a retention/deletion policy for the video and derived data?

questions.l1: No accommodation/validation controls: AI screening is used as-is with inaccessible workflows and no accommodation routing or disability-impact monitoring
questions.l3: Provides an accommodation request channel and some monitoring, but accommodations are slow/manual and validation/monitoring is incomplete
questions.l5: Robust accommodation-by-design with accessible UX, alternative assessment routing, human review SLAs, and ongoing validation/monitoring evidence showing the tool does not disproportionately exclude candidates with disabilities
questions.text: Does the agent implement EEOC-aligned safeguards for AI hiring/selection tools by providing (1) accessible assessment workflows and reasonable accommodation pathways (including alternative assessments and assistive-technology compatibility) and (2) documented validation/monitoring of selection procedures to detect disproportionate exclusion of individuals with disabilities?

questions.l1: No OECD due diligence loop: no structured labor-impact assessment, no worker consultation evidence, and grievances/remediation are not tracked
questions.l3: Performs periodic assessments and tracks some grievances, but consultation and remediation evidence is incomplete and not connected to algorithmic decisions
questions.l5: Full OECD §V operationalization with continuous impact due diligence, documented worker engagement, grievance and remediation case management, and auditable reporting of mitigation effectiveness tied to algorithmic-management changes
questions.text: Does the agent support OECD MNE Guidelines 2023 §V by enabling labor-rights due diligence for algorithmic management (impact identification, prevention/mitigation, worker consultation/engagement, grievance intake, and remediation tracking), with evidence outputs suitable for internal/external accountability?

questions.l1: No applicability matrix; feature rollout does not account for jurisdiction-specific compliance triggers
questions.l3: Maintains a manual policy memo, but gating and evidence retention are inconsistent across teams and releases
questions.l5: Automated scope gating with jurisdiction/role mapping, rollout checks, and evidence bundles demonstrating completion of all location-specific duties prior to deployment
questions.regulatoryRef: Jurisdictional scope gating for employment AI laws
questions.text: Does the program maintain a jurisdictional applicability matrix for employment AI features (e.g., AEDT use in NYC; AI video interview analysis in Illinois), and gate feature rollout on completion of location-specific notice/audit/consent requirements with evidence retention?

questions.l1: Workers and their representatives are not informed before workplace AI is deployed
questions.l3: A generic notice is published, but it is not tied to specific systems, sites or go-live dates
questions.l5: Go-live is gated on a recorded notice to workers' representatives and affected workers for each system and site, with the notice text, date and recipients retained
questions.text: Before a high-risk AI system is put into service or used at the workplace, does the deployer inform workers' representatives and the affected workers that they will be subject to it, as EU AI Act Article 26(7) requires, and keep evidence of the notice?

regulatoryBasis: WEF Future of Jobs Report Framework

regulatoryReferences.citation: ILO Conventions C087 and C098 (freedom of association, collective bargaining)
OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises on Responsible Business Conduct (2023)
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744

regulatoryReferences.text: WEF Future of Jobs Report Framework

sdgAlignment: SDG 8 — Decent Work and Economic Growth

higher-education.certificationPath: L1 Basic academic AI tools → L2 Academic integrity compliance → L3 Full FERPA/accreditation compliant AI governance → L4 AI-enhanced research and pedagogy with ethics oversight → L5 Autonomous higher education AI governance with verified academic outcomes and equity
higher-education.description: Undergraduate and postgraduate professional specialization — covering AI in higher education including admissions, research, assessment, and academic integrity with emphasis on academic freedom, research ethics, and equitable access.
higher-education.euAIActClassification: Annex III §3 — education and vocational training (admission, evaluating learning outcomes, assessing education level, proctoring)
keyRisks: Admissions bias through AI-assisted application screening
Academic integrity erosion from undetectable AI-generated submissions
Research misconduct through AI-fabricated data or results
Student surveillance through AI proctoring and behavioral analytics
Accreditation risk from unvalidated AI-driven curriculum changes
higher-education.name: Higher Education

questions.l1: No admissions bias prevention; AI-assisted application screening is not tested for demographic bias or disparate impact
questions.l3: Agent monitors admissions outcomes by demographic group, but does not implement model-level bias testing or holistic review safeguards
questions.l5: Comprehensive admissions equity with multi-dimensional bias testing, disparate impact analysis, holistic review integration, socioeconomic diversity consideration, transparent selection criteria, and regular third-party equity audit per the EU AI Act
questions.text: Does the agent prevent admissions bias where it is used to determine access or admission to education (EU AI Act Annex III §3(a))?

questions.l1: No research ethics integration; AI-assisted research does not undergo ethics review or comply with human subjects protection requirements
questions.l3: Agent flags research activities that may require IRB review and tracks protocol status, but does not implement AI-specific research ethics assessment
questions.l5: Comprehensive research ethics with AI-specific IRB guidance, automated protocol screening, informed consent management for AI research, data use agreement tracking, and responsible AI research practices per the Common Rule
questions.text: Does the agent implement research ethics compliance per the Common Rule (45 CFR Part 46) and institutional IRB requirements for AI-assisted research?

questions.l1: No AI transparency; students and faculty are not informed about AI system capabilities, limitations, or data usage
questions.l3: Agent provides basic AI usage information and data practices documentation, but does not offer individual-level AI interaction transparency or impact assessment
questions.l5: Full AI transparency with usage dashboards, individual interaction logs, capability/limitation disclosure, data usage transparency, impact assessment reporting, and institutional AI governance documentation per EU AI Act Art. 50
questions.text: Does the agent provide AI usage transparency per EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations and institutional AI disclosure policies?

questions.l1: No academic freedom protection; AI content moderation may restrict legitimate academic discourse or research topics
questions.l3: Agent implements content policies with academic context awareness, but does not systematically protect academic freedom or prevent over-censorship of scholarly content
questions.l5: Full academic freedom protection with scholarly context recognition, research topic protection, academic discourse preservation, content policy academic exceptions, and transparent content moderation appeals per UNESCO recommendations
questions.regulatoryRef: UNESCO Recommendation on HE Teaching Personnel (1997) §27-29
questions.text: Does the agent protect academic freedom per UNESCO Recommendation on Higher Education Teaching Personnel and prevent AI-driven censorship of research?

questions.l1: No data portability; student records and credentials are not exportable in interoperable formats
questions.l3: Agent supports basic transcript export, but not in a structured, machine-readable format, or not transmittable to another institution
questions.l5: Full data portability per GDPR Art. 20 with machine-readable export of student-provided data, direct transmission to another institution where technically feasible, transcript interoperability, and logged export requests
questions.text: Does the agent implement student data portability per GDPR Article 20, exporting the data a student provided in a structured, machine-readable format that can be transmitted to another institution?

questions.l1: Misconduct findings are issued automatically from proctoring flags
questions.l3: Flags are reviewed by staff, but students cannot see or respond to the flagged evidence
questions.l5: No finding issues without a recorded human decision; students receive the flagged evidence and can respond; flag rates are compared across student groups each term
questions.text: During online exam proctoring (EU AI Act Annex III point 3(d)), does every misconduct flag the agent raises go to a human decision-maker, with the student able to see and respond to the flagged evidence?

questions.l1: Exams and proctoring rules are the same for every student; approved adjustments are not applied
questions.l3: Approved adjustments are applied manually and inconsistently, or proctoring rules ignore them
questions.l5: Each approved adjustment is recorded per student and applied automatically to exam format and monitoring rules before the exam; application is logged; flag and failure rates are compared across disability groups each term
questions.text: When the agent administers, proctors or scores course examinations, are evaluation methods adjusted for students with a disability that impairs sensory, manual or speaking skills, so that results reflect achievement rather than the impairment (Section 504, 34 CFR §104.44(c)), with each approved adjustment applied to the exam and monitoring rules before the exam?

questions.l1: Annex III point 3 uses are not inventoried; no risk-management record or oversight design exists
questions.l3: Admissions use has a risk-management record and human review, but evaluation, placement or proctoring uses lack them, or overseers cannot override or stop the system
questions.l5: Every Annex III point 3 use is inventoried; each has a maintained Art. 9 risk-management record and an Art. 14(4) oversight design (understand limits, guard against automation bias, interpret, override, stop) with tested override and stop paths and post-market monitoring evidence
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Annex III §3; EU AI Act Art. 9; EU AI Act Art. 14(4); EU AI Act Art. 113 (as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
questions.text: For each high-risk education use of the agent listed in EU AI Act Annex III point 3 — (a) admission or assignment, (b) evaluating learning outcomes, (c) assessing the level of education, (d) monitoring prohibited behaviour during tests — is there a maintained Art. 9 risk-management record and an Art. 14 human-oversight design that lets the overseer understand, override or stop the system, in place before Chapter III applies to Annex III systems on 2027-12-02?

questions.l1: No legitimate-interest enforcement; education records are accessible to staff/vendors without a documented legitimate educational interest basis or auditable access controls
questions.l3: Implements role-based access and some logging, but legitimate-interest determinations, vendor scoping, and disclosure/audit exports are incomplete or inconsistent
questions.l5: End-to-end §99.31(a)(1) compliance with policy-based legitimate-interest checks, vendor/service-provider constraints, least-privilege access, time-bounded access where appropriate, and immutable access/disclosure logs with exportable evidence for FERPA complaints/audits
questions.text: Does the agent implement FERPA 34 CFR §99.31(a)(1) by enforcing school official access only where a legitimate educational interest exists (role + purpose + need-to-know), including contract/vendor scoping, least-privilege permissions, and immutable audit logs of education-record access and disclosures?

questions.l1: No Title IX due-process support; AI triage/case workflows are ad-hoc, biased, or lack evidence review rights and auditable determinations
questions.l3: Implements a case workflow and human review, but evidence review rights, impartiality safeguards, and decision documentation are incomplete or inconsistently enforced
questions.l5: Full §106.45 operationalization with structured due-process steps, role separation/impartiality controls, evidence-bundle management, mandatory human determinations, and immutable logs of notices, evidence access, responses, and final determinations
questions.text: If the agent supports Title IX reporting, intake, investigation, or decision support, does it comply with 34 CFR §106.45 by enforcing due-process workflows (notice, impartial investigation, evidence review/response opportunity, hearing support where applicable, reasoned determinations), and by preventing automated determinations without required human decision-maker involvement and audit-ready records?

questions.l1: Detector scores alone produce misconduct findings; no published AI-use rules per assessment
questions.l3: AI-use rules exist, but detector output is treated as conclusive or students have no appeal before a finding
questions.l5: AI-use and attribution rules are published per assessment; detector output is recorded as one input to a human decision; findings follow a documented process with notice, response and appeal; cases are reviewed each term for detector false positives
questions.regulatoryRef: Institutional academic integrity policy (no binding instrument identified)
questions.text: Does the agent support the institution's academic-integrity policy on generative AI — published AI-use and attribution rules per assessment, detector output used only as one input to a human decision, and notice, response and appeal before any misconduct finding?

questions.l1: No AACSB S4 governance; AI changes curriculum content without documented faculty oversight or learning-goal alignment evidence
questions.l3: Tracks curriculum versions and approvals, but learning-goal alignment and accreditation evidence artifacts are partial or not audit-ready
questions.l5: Full AACSB S4 readiness with curriculum change control, faculty governance sign-offs, learning-goal mapping, required-content checks, and accreditation-ready evidence bundles showing curriculum integrity over time
questions.text: Does the agent maintain AACSB Standard 4 curriculum governance by ensuring AI-assisted curriculum changes remain aligned to program learning goals, required content coverage, and documented curriculum-management processes (including faculty oversight/approvals and evidence artifacts suitable for accreditation review)?

questions.l1: Education records are reused for analytics or research with no de-identification or studies-exception basis recorded
questions.l3: De-identification is applied, but the re-identification review, approvals or dataset access logs are incomplete
questions.l5: Each secondary-use dataset records its basis (§99.31(b)(1) de-identified release or §99.31(a)(6) studies disclosure), a re-identification review, approval, provenance and access logs
questions.text: When education records are used for analytics or research, does the agent release them only as de-identified data after removal of all personally identifiable information (34 CFR §99.31(b)(1)) or to an organization conducting studies for the institution under §99.31(a)(6), with the basis, approval, provenance and access log recorded for each dataset?

questions.l1: No WCAG 2.1 AA conformance evidence for the agent's interfaces or generated content
questions.l3: Interfaces are audited to WCAG 2.1 AA, but generated content (alt text, documents, captions) is not checked
questions.l5: WCAG 2.1 A/AA testing of interfaces and generated content runs each release with assistive-technology checks; a conformance report per release; defects tracked to remediation before the compliance date
questions.text: For deployments by or for a public college or university, do the agent's web and mobile interfaces and the content it generates meet WCAG 2.1 Level A and AA under the ADA Title II rule (28 CFR §35.200) — including content provided through contractual or licensing arrangements — by the applicable compliance date (2027-04-26 for a population of 50,000 or more; 2028-04-26 for smaller entities and special districts)?

questions.l1: Students are not told a high-risk AI system is used; no explanation channel
questions.l3: A general notice exists, but individual explanations are unavailable or do not state the system's role and the main elements of the decision
questions.l5: Notice at the point of decision; an explanation-on-request workflow with a response deadline; explanations generated from logged decision inputs; request and response records kept
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 26(11); EU AI Act Art. 86
questions.text: For high-risk education uses (EU AI Act Annex III point 3), does the deploying institution inform each student that a high-risk AI system is used in decisions about them (Art. 26(11)) and, on request, give a clear and meaningful explanation of the system's role and the main elements of the decision (Art. 86), in place by 2027-12-02?

questions.l1: No fundamental rights impact assessment or DPIA
questions.l3: A DPIA exists, but Art. 27(1) elements (affected groups, oversight, complaint mechanisms) are missing
questions.l5: A fundamental rights impact assessment covering Art. 27(1)(a)-(f), cross-referenced to any existing DPIA, completed before first use and updated on material change

questions.l1: No systemic risk assessment; content recommendation does not assess fundamental rights impacts, civic discourse, or public security risks per DSA Art. 34

questions.l3: Agent tracks software versions and maintains change documentation, but does not implement full IEC 62304 quality management system integration
questions.l5: Full IEC 62304 QMS integration with software safety classification, development planning per Clause 5.1, requirements management, architecture documentation, verification/validation, release management, and maintenance process per Clause 6
questions.text: Does the agent implement software lifecycle management per IEC 62304:2006/AMD1:2015 Clause 4 quality management system requirements for health software?

questions.l1: No Part 11 compliance; electronic health records lack required controls for data integrity and electronic signatures
questions.l3: Agent implements basic audit trails and access controls per §11.10, but electronic signatures and system validation are not fully compliant
questions.l5: Full Part 11 compliance with validated systems, complete audit trails per §11.10(e), electronic signatures per §11.50/§11.70, system access controls, authority checks, device checks, and periodic system validation documentation
questions.text: Does the agent enforce electronic records integrity per FDA 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10 controls for closed systems including audit trails and electronic signatures?

questions.l1: No AI explainability; health predictions and recommendations are black-box with no explanation of reasoning
questions.l3: Agent provides basic explanations of AI outputs and confidence levels, but does not implement detailed feature attribution or uncertainty quantification
questions.l5: Full health AI explainability with feature attribution, uncertainty quantification, confidence calibration, counterfactual explanations, clinician-appropriate and patient-appropriate explanation modes, and transparency documentation per EU AI Act Art. 13
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 13; FDA AI/ML Transparency Principles
questions.text: Does the agent provide health AI explainability per EU AI Act Article 13 transparency requirements and FDA Transparency Principles for AI/ML?

questions.l1: No health-specific cybersecurity; digital health systems use generic security controls without medical device threat modeling
questions.l3: SBOM and a vulnerability process exist, but the agent's model, prompt and tool dependencies are not in the SBOM or threat model
questions.l5: SBOM covers the agent including model and tool dependencies; threat model and security risk assessment are linked to safety risk management; postmarket vulnerability monitoring and coordinated disclosure are evidenced
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA Cybersecurity in Medical Devices guidance (February 2026); FD&C Act §524B; IEC 81001-5-1
questions.text: For cyber devices, does the agent's manufacturer provide the FD&C Act §524B evidence (SBOM, postmarket vulnerability monitoring plan, secure product development framework) per FDA's cybersecurity guidance (February 2026), with IEC 81001-5-1 health software security activities?

questions.l1: Model and prompt changes ship without regulatory change assessment
questions.l3: A PCCP covers model retraining, but prompt and tool changes are outside it
questions.l5: The PCCP covers every modifiable component; each change record shows it was executed per the modification protocol with impact assessment; changes outside the PCCP trigger a new submission decision
questions.regulatoryRef: 21 U.S.C. 360e-4; FDA PCCP for AI-Enabled Device Software Functions final guidance
questions.text: Does the agent's manufacturer control AI changes through an authorized predetermined change control plan (21 U.S.C. 360e-4; FDA PCCP final guidance) describing the planned modifications, the methodology to develop, validate and implement them, and an impact assessment, covering every modifiable component including prompts and tools?

questions.l1: No HTA readiness; digital health technologies are not assessed for clinical and economic value
questions.l3: Outcome data is collected, but it is not structured for HTA submission or JCA scope is not assessed
questions.l5: JCA scope under Art. 7 is assessed and recorded; comparative effectiveness and patient-reported outcome evidence is structured for HTA bodies; evidence gaps are tracked
questions.regulatoryRef: Regulation (EU) 2021/2282 Art. 7; NICE ESF for DHTs
questions.text: Does the agent's evidence generation support health technology assessment, including joint clinical assessment where the technology falls under Regulation (EU) 2021/2282 Art. 7?

questions.l1: No CDS boundary classification; AI health apps operate without FDA CDS guidance Non-Device vs Device classification assessment, risking unregulated SaMD deployment
questions.l3: Functions are classified once, but the record does not address each criterion or is not repeated after feature changes
questions.l5: Each function has a dated classification record addressing every criterion; feature changes trigger re-classification; device functions follow a regulatory pathway
questions.regulatoryRef: FD&C Act §520(o)(1)(E); FDA Clinical Decision Support Software guidance (January 2026)
questions.text: Does the agent's provider classify each decision-support function as non-device CDS or device software using the FD&C Act §520(o)(1)(E) criteria as explained in FDA's CDS guidance (January 2026), and re-run the classification when features change?

questions.l1: No software requirements analysis; system behavior is implicit and tests are not traceable to safety requirements
questions.l3: Partial requirements exist with some test links, but risk-control linkage, coverage checks, and change impact analysis are incomplete
questions.l5: Full §5.2 compliance with controlled requirements, traceability completeness checks, risk-control linkage, change impact analysis, and release gating on trace completeness
questions.text: Does the agent support software requirements analysis per IEC 62304:2006 §5.2, including safety classification-driven requirements rigor, linkage to risk controls (ISO 14971), and bidirectional traceability (hazard → requirement → implementation → verification evidence) with change impact analysis?

questions.l1: No performance evaluation; diagnostic claims are made without structured evidence or monitoring
questions.l3: Some validation evidence exists, but it is not structured as an IVDR-grade performance evaluation with clear intended purpose alignment and ongoing monitoring
questions.l5: Comprehensive IVDR-grade performance evaluation support with plan/report structures, analytical + clinical performance evidence linkage, intended-purpose traceability, and post-market performance monitoring with drift triggers
questions.regulatoryRef: EU IVDR 2017/746 Art. 56; EU IVDR 2017/746 Annex XIII
questions.text: If the agent makes diagnostic or IVD-adjacent claims or interprets biomarker inputs, does it support IVDR performance evaluation evidence (EU IVDR 2017/746 Art. 56; Annex XIII), including a performance evaluation plan, scientific validity and analytical and clinical performance evidence, and post-market performance follow-up?

questions.l1: No structured clinical evaluation; claims are not supported by clinical association/analytical/clinical validation evidence
questions.l3: Some validation exists, but evidence is fragmented and does not cleanly map to clinical association vs analytical vs clinical validation for the intended use
questions.l5: Full clinical evaluation with evidence mapping, intended-use traceability, subgroup performance analysis, and continuous real-world performance feedback into evaluation updates
questions.text: Does the agent implement the FDA guidance Software as a Medical Device (SaMD): Clinical Evaluation by structuring evidence as (1) valid clinical association, (2) analytical validation and (3) clinical validation, with intended-use alignment, subgroup analysis and real-world performance monitoring?

questions.l1: No interoperability safety controls; device data is ingested without semantic/unit/time validation
questions.l3: Basic device integration exists, but semantic/unit/time-sync validation and auditability are incomplete
questions.l5: Robust IEEE 11073-10201-aligned interoperability with semantic/unit/time validation, transport resilience, provenance logs, and safety checks that gate downstream clinical logic on data integrity
questions.text: Does the agent ensure safe interoperability for connected health devices by implementing IEEE 11073-10201-aligned data exchange (device identity, measurement semantics/units, time synchronization, transport constraints), plus validation checks and audit logs to prevent silent data misinterpretation?

material-to-machines.certificationPath: L1 Basic material compliance tracking → L2 RoHS/WEEE compliance automation → L3 Full ecodesign integration per EU Regulation 2024/1781 → L4 Circular economy optimization with DPP → L5 Autonomous product lifecycle governance with verified sustainability metrics
material-to-machines.description: Appliances, quality of life improvement, and manufacturing — covering the lifecycle of consumer and industrial products from raw material extraction through design, manufacturing, use, and end-of-life with emphasis on ecodesign, energy efficiency, and circular economy principles.
material-to-machines.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III; high-risk only under Art. 6(1) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a product covered by Annex I legislation — otherwise Art. 4 (AI literacy), Art. 5 (prohibited practices) and Art. 50 (transparency) apply
keyRisks: Conflict mineral sourcing undetected in AI-optimized procurement
Planned obsolescence embedded in AI-driven product design
Hazardous substance threshold violations in automated material substitution
Energy efficiency rating manipulation through selective testing conditions
E-waste export to developing nations through logistics optimization
material-to-machines.name: Material to Machines

questions.l1: No RoHS screening; component selection does not verify restricted substance concentrations against Annex II thresholds
questions.l3: Agent screens components against RoHS Annex II substance limits (lead, mercury, cadmium, Cr6+, PBB, PBDE, DEHP, BBP, DBP, DIBP) but relies on supplier declarations without independent verification
questions.l5: Every component is screened against Annex II maximum concentration values with supplier declarations and test (e.g. XRF) evidence linked, exemptions under Annex III/IV are tracked with expiry dates, and components without evidence cannot be released
questions.text: Does the agent enforce restricted substance compliance per RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU Annex II maximum concentration values for all electrical/electronic components?

questions.l1: No ecodesign integration; product design decisions do not consider repairability, durability, or end-of-life recyclability
questions.l3: Agent evaluates designs against ecodesign criteria and generates repairability scores, but does not actively optimize designs for circular economy outcomes
questions.l5: Full ecodesign optimization engine that balances performance, cost, repairability (per repair score methodology), durability testing predictions, recyclability assessment, and material efficiency — with automated compliance documentation per Art. 5
questions.text: Does the agent implement ecodesign requirements per EU Ecodesign Regulation 2024/1781 Article 5 including repairability, durability, and recyclability criteria?

questions.l1: No WEEE tracking; producer responsibility obligations are managed manually with no visibility into collection or recycling rates
questions.l3: Agent tracks WEEE registration and reports collection volumes, but does not optimize reverse logistics or monitor recycling target achievement in real-time
questions.l5: Comprehensive WEEE lifecycle management with automated producer registration across jurisdictions, real-time collection rate monitoring against Art. 7 targets, recycling process optimization, and material recovery tracking with verified evidence
questions.text: Does the agent manage WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU Article 12 producer responsibility obligations including collection rate tracking and recycling target compliance?

questions.l1: No energy-label generation or EPREL registration support
questions.l3: Labels are generated from test results, but EPREL registration and test-report linkage are manual
questions.l5: Every model has its label and information sheet generated from linked test reports under the applicable delegated regulation, EPREL registration is completed before release, and label changes are versioned
questions.text: Does the agent generate energy labels and product information sheets from test results under the applicable delegated regulation and register each model in EPREL before it is placed on the market, per Regulation (EU) 2017/1369?

questions.l1: No conflict mineral tracking; 3TG sourcing is not assessed for conflict-affected or high-risk area origins
questions.l3: Agent collects Conflict Minerals Reporting Templates (CMRTs) from suppliers and flags high-risk smelters, but does not perform independent supply chain due diligence per OECD guidance
questions.l5: Full conflict mineral due diligence with smelter-level traceability, OECD 5-step framework implementation, automated CMRT collection and validation, risk assessment for all CAHRAs, and transparent reporting per Art. 7
questions.text: Does the agent implement conflict mineral due diligence per EU Conflict Minerals Regulation 2017/821 Article 4 for tin, tantalum, tungsten, and gold (3TG)?

questions.l1: No DPP capability; product information is not structured for machine-readable access
questions.l3: Agent generates basic DPPs with material composition and compliance data, but interoperability with EU DPP infrastructure and data carrier standards is incomplete
questions.l5: For each product group with an adopted delegated act, every mandatory DPP attribute is populated with a source-evidence link, the data carrier resolves to the current record, lifecycle updates are versioned, and consumer and recycler views are available
questions.text: Does the agent maintain Digital Product Passport data per Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 Art. 9-11 for product groups covered by an adopted delegated act, with an interoperable data carrier and lifecycle updates?

questions.l1: No lifecycle impact assessment; environmental considerations are not integrated into design decisions
questions.l3: Agent performs simplified LCA using industry databases and identifies major environmental hotspots, but does not systematically apply IEC 62430 design principles
questions.l5: Comprehensive environmentally conscious design integration with full LCA per ISO 14044, design optimization against multiple environmental indicators, material selection guidance per IEC 62430, and verified impact reduction tracking
questions.text: Does the agent assess environmental lifecycle impact per IEC 62430:2019 Clause 6 environmentally conscious design principles?

questions.l1: No battery-specific compliance; battery components are treated generically without regulation-specific tracking
questions.l3: Agent tracks battery chemistry and capacity for classification, generates carbon footprint declarations per Art. 7, but does not manage full lifecycle obligations including collection and recycling
questions.l5: End-to-end battery compliance with carbon footprint calculation per delegated methodology, recycled content verification per Art. 8, performance/durability tracking per Art. 10, battery passport generation per Art. 77, and second-life assessment
questions.text: Does the agent manage battery compliance per EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542 Articles 7-11 including carbon footprint declaration and recycled content requirements?

questions.l1: No zone/conduit model or target security level for systems the agent touches
questions.l3: Zones and conduits are defined and basic access controls applied, but achieved security level is not assessed against SL-T
questions.l5: Each zone and conduit has a documented SL-T, the achieved level is assessed against the IEC 62443-3-3 system requirements with gaps tracked, and agent changes to OT systems are re-assessed before deployment
questions.text: Does the agent's deployment in industrial control systems meet the target security level (SL-T) for its zones and conduits per IEC 62443-3-3:2013 system security requirements?

questions.l1: No EHSR mapping; safety functions changed by software or ML updates are not re-assessed
questions.l3: An EHSR checklist exists and major updates are reviewed, but ML/software updates to safety functions are not consistently gated
questions.l5: Every update touching a safety function passes a recorded EHSR impact assessment before release, self-evolving safety components have a notified-body assessment plan, and the technical documentation is updated per release
questions.regulatoryRef: Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 Art. 10, Annex III (EHSR), Annex I Part A
questions.text: Where the agent's software or ML model performs or changes a machinery safety function, does each update re-assess conformity with the essential health and safety requirements (Annex III) before release, and is third-party conformity assessment planned for safety components with self-evolving behaviour, per Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (applies 20 Jan 2027)?

questions.l1: Shared accounts/weak authentication; device/service identities are unmanaged and not auditable
questions.l3: Unique user IDs and basic authentication are implemented, but service/device identity, credential rotation, and coverage across zones is incomplete
questions.l5: Full SR 1.1 implementation with unique identities for users/services/devices, strong authentication, credential rotation, secure enrollment, continuous verification, and audit-ready evidence mapped to target security level
questions.text: Does the agent implement and continuously verify Identification and Authentication Control per IEC 62443-3-3 SR 1.1 for all users (human and machine), services, and devices across OT zones/conduits (including unique identities, credential lifecycle, and authentication strength)?

questions.l1: No formal change management for OH&S; changes are applied without documented hazard/risk review
questions.l3: Performs change reviews and risk assessments for major changes, but coverage is inconsistent and worker consultation/evidence capture is incomplete
questions.l5: Closed-loop OH&S change management with automated hazard prompts, risk controls selection, worker consultation records, pre-startup safety verification, and auditable change approval gates
questions.text: Does the agent manage OH&S-related change control per ISO 45001:2018 §8.1.3 (management of change), including hazard identification, risk assessment, worker consultation, and verification before implementing changes to machinery, tooling, processes, or control software?

questions.l1: No repairability controls; design decisions do not manage spare parts, disassembly, or repair information availability
questions.l3: Generates repairability guidance and partial spare-parts lists, but compliance is not enforced as a release gate and evidence is incomplete
questions.l5: Repairability-by-design with enforceable constraints, automated spare-parts availability rules, disassembly time/steps scoring, repair information publication workflows, and compliance evidence packs aligned to delegated-act requirements
questions.text: Does the agent apply the repairability parameters set under Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 Art. 5(1) and the related Art. 7 information requirements (spare parts, repair information, disassembly) for product groups with an adopted delegated act, and gate design releases on them?

questions.l1: No release gate; products are placed on the market without consolidated RoHS compliance evidence and exemption control
questions.l3: Aggregates BOM declarations and flags issues, but exemption applicability and product-level sign-off are manual and inconsistently retained
questions.l5: Automated product-level RoHS compliance gating with evidence linkage, exemption lifecycle management (Annex III/IV), sampling/testing integration, and audit-ready technical file exports
questions.text: Does the agent enforce RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU Article 4 by gating release/placing-on-the-market decisions on product-level RoHS compliance evidence (including BOM aggregation, supplier declarations, test evidence, and exemption applicability tracking)?

questions.l1: No treatment information is published for new equipment types
questions.l3: Treatment information exists for some product lines but is not linked to product types or launch dates
questions.l5: Per-type treatment records generated from the bill of materials, published to treatment facilities within one year of market placement, versioned on design changes and cross-checked with the Digital Product Passport
questions.text: Does the agent provide treatment facilities with the reuse and treatment information required by WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU Article 15 (components, materials and the location of dangerous substances) for each new type of electrical and electronic equipment within one year of placing it on the market?

questions.l1: No path to report vulnerabilities or incidents in agent-managed products
questions.l3: A manual reporting path to the Single Reporting Platform exists, but timing has not been tested
questions.l5: Detection-to-report is rehearsed and timed against 24h/72h, final-report content (corrective measure, root cause) is assembled from agent and product logs, and each report is retained
questions.regulatoryRef: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (manufacturer reporting of actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents)
questions.text: Can the manufacturer report an actively exploited vulnerability or severe incident affecting a connected product the agent runs on or manages through the CRA Single Reporting Platform within the Cyber Resilience Act deadlines (24h early warning, 72h notification, final report) applying from 11 Sep 2026?

networked-ecosystems.certificationPath: L1 Basic API security → L2 GDPR data portability compliance → L3 EU Data Act/DGA compliance → L4 Full ecosystem trust architecture → L5 Autonomous ecosystem orchestration with verified data rights and sovereignty
networked-ecosystems.description: Data connectivity across customer, enterprise, and industry ecosystems — flipping financial ecosystems to human ecosystems — AI agents orchestrating data flows, API ecosystems, and platform integrations with emphasis on interoperability, data rights, and ecosystem trust.
networked-ecosystems.euAIActClassification: Annex III §2 where a safety component of critical digital infrastructure; otherwise not listed — Art. 50 transparency applies
keyRisks: Data sovereignty erosion through ecosystem lock-in
API abuse enabling unauthorized data aggregation
Ecosystem monopolization through AI-managed data access
Privacy violations through ecosystem data correlation
Critical infrastructure dependency on single ecosystem providers
networked-ecosystems.name: Connectivity to Networked Ecosystems

questions.l1: No Data Act compliance; product-generated data is not accessible to users or third parties per Chapter II requirements
questions.l3: Agent supports basic data access requests per EU Data Act, but does not implement automated portability, third-party sharing obligations, or data holder compliance documentation
questions.l5: Full EU Data Act compliance with automated product data access per Art. 4, portability API per Art. 5, third-party sharing governance per Art. 6-8, data holder compliance documentation, and real-time data access logging
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Data Act 2023/2854 Ch. II Art. 4-8
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Data Act 2023/2854 Chapter II data access rights including product data access, portability, and third-party data sharing obligations?

questions.l1: No systematic API security; APIs expose data without authorization controls, rate limiting, or security configuration management
questions.l3: Agent implements authentication and basic authorization for APIs, but does not systematically address all OWASP API Top 10 vulnerabilities or perform API security testing
questions.l5: Full OWASP API Security Top 10 mitigation with automated vulnerability scanning, broken object-level authorization enforcement, API gateway security configuration, rate limiting, injection prevention, and continuous API security monitoring
questions.text: Does the agent implement API security per OWASP API Security Top 10 2023 including broken object level authorization (API1) and security misconfiguration (API8) prevention?

questions.l1: No data intermediary governance; ecosystem data sharing lacks DGA Chapter III requirements for neutrality, transparency, and registration
questions.l3: Agent implements basic data sharing transparency and neutrality controls, but does not meet full DGA Art. 10-15 requirements for registered data intermediary services
questions.l5: Full DGA Chapter III compliance with data intermediary registration, neutrality enforcement, transparent service terms, data subject rights support, separation of intermediary and other activities, and competent authority notification
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Data Governance Act 2022/868 Ch. III Art. 10-15
questions.text: Does the agent implement data intermediary compliance per EU Data Governance Act 2022/868 Chapter III requirements for data sharing services?

questions.l1: No portability implementation; personal data cannot be exported by users in machine-readable formats per GDPR Art. 20 or CCPA requirements
questions.l3: Agent supports basic data export functionality, but does not implement full GDPR Art. 20 direct transmission or maintain comprehensive data portability across all data categories
questions.l5: Full portability with automated GDPR Art. 20 structured export, direct controller-to-controller transmission, CCPA data download support, interoperable format standardization, and portability request tracking with statutory deadline enforcement
questions.text: Does the agent enforce data portability per GDPR Article 20 and CCPA §1798.100(d) with automated structured data export in interoperable formats?

questions.l1: No open standards; ecosystem integration uses proprietary APIs and formats creating vendor lock-in and interoperability barriers
questions.l3: Agent implements OpenAPI documentation and standard authentication protocols, but does not apply EU EIF technical interoperability principles across all ecosystem connections
questions.l5: Full open standards implementation with OpenAPI 3.1 documentation, EU EIF technical layer compliance, W3C semantic interoperability, vendor lock-in prevention measures, and ecosystem diversity monitoring
questions.regulatoryRef: W3C Standards; OpenAPI 3.1; EU EIF v2
questions.text: Does the agent implement open standards for ecosystem connectivity per W3C Web standards, OpenAPI 3.1, and EU Interoperability Framework (EIF) technical interoperability layer?

questions.l1: No identity federation; ecosystem access uses siloed identity systems without federation standards or assurance level verification
questions.l3: Agent implements OAuth 2.0 authorization and basic OIDC federation, but does not enforce NIST SP 800-63-3 assurance levels or implement step-up authentication for sensitive ecosystem operations
questions.l5: Full identity federation with OIDC/OAuth 2.1 implementation, NIST SP 800-63-3 IAL/AAL enforcement, step-up authentication for sensitive operations, federation trust framework documentation, and continuous identity assurance monitoring
questions.text: Does the agent implement identity federation per OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.1 and NIST SP 800-63-3 identity assurance levels for ecosystem access management?

questions.l1: No ecosystem trust framework; participant verification and trust establishment are informal without standards-based trust anchors
questions.l3: Agent validates ecosystem participant certificates and maintains trust anchors, but does not implement full eIDAS 2.0 qualified trust service requirements or ENISA trust framework
questions.l5: Full ecosystem trust governance with eIDAS 2.0 qualified trust service integration, PKI management, trust anchor maintenance, ecosystem participant verification, qualified electronic signature support, and trust framework audit trail
questions.text: Does the agent implement ecosystem trust governance per ENISA Cybersecurity for Connected and Automated Mobility and EU eIDAS 2.0 trust service requirements?

questions.l1: No algorithmic transparency; ecosystem ranking, access, and data monetization decisions are opaque without fairness assessment
questions.l3: Agent provides basic transparency reports for ecosystem ranking and access decisions, but does not implement full DMA Art. 6(12) requirements or contestability mechanisms
questions.l5: Full DMA compliance with algorithmic transparency for ranking and access decisions, non-discrimination monitoring, business user access audits, contestability mechanisms, and transparent data access pricing per EU Data Act Art. 33
questions.regulatoryRef: EU DMA Art. 6(12); EU Data Act Art. 33
questions.text: Does the agent implement algorithmic transparency per EU Digital Markets Act Article 6(12) for core platform services and fair access principles?

questions.l1: No DMA algorithmic transparency or Data Act pricing compliance; AI ecosystem agents manage ranking and data access without DMA Art. 6(12) transparency or Art. 33 fair pricing requirements
questions.l3: Agent provides basic transparency for ecosystem ranking decisions, but does not implement DMA Art. 6(12) full algorithmic transparency requirements or EU Data Act Art. 33 fair data access pricing
questions.l5: Full DMA Art. 6(12) algorithmic transparency with ranking parameter disclosure, non-discrimination monitoring, EU Data Act Art. 33 fair data access pricing, FRAND-equivalent terms for ecosystem data, and contestability mechanisms for AI-managed access decisions
questions.regulatoryRef: EU DMA Art. 6(12); EU Data Act Art. 33
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Digital Markets Act Article 6(12) algorithmic transparency for core platform services and EU Data Act Article 33 fair data access pricing for AI-managed ecosystem data monetization?

questions.l1: No PKCE enforcement; authorization code flows can proceed without code_challenge / code_verifier or allow insecure downgrade, and evidence is missing
questions.l3: PKCE is implemented for some clients, but enforcement is inconsistent (e.g., legacy exceptions), redirect/state handling is incomplete, or evidence is not audit-ready
questions.l5: Full OAuth 2.1 §4.1 PKCE enforcement (S256) for all public clients, strict redirect URI + state/nonce validation, downgrade prevention, continuous conformance testing, and immutable audit logs demonstrating PKCE policy compliance
questions.text: Does the agent implement OAuth 2.1 authorization code flow with PKCE per OAuth 2.1 §4.1 (S256), including strict redirect URI matching, state/nonce anti-CSRF protections, prevention of PKCE downgrade, and auditable evidence (logs/telemetry) that PKCE is enforced for all public clients?

questions.l1: No Art. 12 controls; intermediary operations are commingled, data may be reused for other purposes, and evidence is missing
questions.l3: Some neutrality/separation controls exist, but segregation, security measures, and audit evidence are incomplete or inconsistently enforced across services/partners
questions.l5: Full Art. 12 implementation with enforced non-use constraints, operational separation, technical/organizational controls, continuous monitoring, and audit-ready evidence bundles aligned to competent authority expectations
questions.text: If the agent provides data intermediation services, does it operationalize DGA Art. 12 by enforcing neutrality and separation (no data use for other purposes, ring-fenced operations), implementing appropriate technical and organizational measures for secure intermediation, and maintaining audit-ready evidence (policies, access logs, segregation controls, and periodic compliance attestations)?

questions.l1: No object-level authorization; endpoints rely on client-provided identifiers without ownership/tenant checks and lack authorization tests
questions.l3: Implements some object/tenant checks, but coverage is inconsistent, authorization logic is duplicated, or test evidence is incomplete
questions.l5: Full API1 prevention with centralized authorization, consistent ownership/tenant checks, automated authZ test suites per endpoint/resource, and audit-ready access decision logs
questions.text: Does the agent prevent OWASP API1 (Broken Object Level Authorization) by enforcing object ownership/tenant isolation on every object access, using centralized authorization (policy enforcement points), and maintaining automated authorization test coverage (positive/negative cases) with logs suitable for incident reconstruction?

questions.l1: Access is ad hoc/manual; interfaces are insecure or slow, and timeliness/continuity evidence is missing
questions.l3: Access interfaces exist, but timeliness/continuity SLAs and evidence are incomplete or inconsistently met
questions.l5: Full Art. 4 operationalization with secure interfaces, timeliness/continuity controls, SLA monitoring, and audit-ready access evidence bundles
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Data Act Art. 4 access obligations in an operationally usable way (secure access interface, timely/continuous access where applicable, SLA evidence for no undue delay, and audit logs proving access was provided to users upon request)?

questions.l1: Users cannot access the data their product generates
questions.l3: Data is available on request through support, not directly or by default
questions.l5: Direct, default access in a structured, machine-readable format, with metadata, free of charge, verified for each product line placed on the market after 12 September 2026
questions.text: For connected products placed on the market after 12 September 2026, are product data and related service data accessible to the user by default, easily, securely and free of charge, as EU Data Act 2023/2854 Article 3(1) requires?

questions.l1: Third-party APIs and SDKs are adopted without security review
questions.l3: Major suppliers are reviewed at onboarding, but transitive dependencies and changes are not tracked
questions.l5: Dependency inventory including transitive components, security requirements in supplier agreements, change monitoring, and documented exit paths for critical suppliers
questions.text: Does the ecosystem operator manage information security risks in the ICT supply chain of the APIs, SDKs and services the agent depends on, consistent with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A control 5.21?

Data exploitation of vulnerable population financial behavior

questions.l3: Agent implements basic affordability checks and interest rate monitoring, but does not assess cumulative debt burden or prevent over-indebtedness across multiple lenders

questions.text: Does the agent prevent predatory lending per CGAP Client Protection Principles and World Bank Good Practices for Financial Consumer Protection?
