questions.l5: Every data-sharing term set is screened against the Article 13 list of unfair terms, findings are routed to legal with the clause cited, and the review outcome is retained
questions.text: Does the agent screen data-sharing terms proposed to or by partner enterprises for unfair contractual terms under EU Data Act 2023/2854 Article 13, and flag unilaterally imposed terms on data access and use for legal review?

regulatoryReferences.citation: WIPO Copyright Treaty and WIPO Internet Treaties (1996)

patient-lifecycle.certificationPath: L1 Basic appointment scheduling → L2 Clinical workflow automation with safety checks → L3 Full care coordination with JCI-aligned quality → L4 Predictive clinical decision support with FDA compliance → L5 Autonomous patient lifecycle orchestration with verified clinical outcomes
patient-lifecycle.description: Appointment through investigation, diagnosis, treatment, care, and prognosis — covering the complete patient journey with emphasis on clinical safety, informed consent, care coordination, and outcome measurement.
patient-lifecycle.euAIActClassification: Art. 6(1) and Annex I (Regulation (EU) 2017/745 MDR, 2017/746 IVDR) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a medical device; Annex III §5(d) for emergency healthcare patient triage; §5(a) for public-authority eligibility decisions on healthcare services
keyRisks: Misdiagnosis from AI clinical decision support without adequate validation
Treatment delay from automated triage errors
Informed consent violations through AI-mediated patient communication
Care fragmentation from poor AI-managed handoff between providers
Prognostic model bias leading to disparate care quality across demographics
patient-lifecycle.name: Patient Lifecycle

questions.l1: Opaque recommendations, including time-critical alerts, are offered as non-device CDS
questions.l3: Basis information is available on request but is not patient-specific, and time-criticality is not assessed
questions.l5: Each recommendation shows its patient-specific basis; an intended-use and time-criticality analysis is on file; automation-bias usability testing is recorded; functions that fail the criteria follow the device pathway
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA Clinical Decision Support Software guidance (January 2026)
questions.text: Does the agent keep non-device CDS status by letting health care professionals independently review the basis of each recommendation (inputs, data relied on, validation, patient-specific unknowns), and treat time-critical or judgment-directing uses as device functions (FDA CDS guidance, January 2026)?

questions.l1: No digital consent management; informed consent is paper-based with no AI-specific disclosures about automated decision-making in care
questions.l3: Agent generates digital consent forms with AI disclosure language and tracks consent status, but does not support dynamic consent for evolving AI involvement or multilingual accessibility
questions.l5: Comprehensive informed consent with AI-specific disclosures per JCI PCC.4, dynamic consent for changing AI involvement, multilingual support, health literacy-appropriate language, consent verification at each care stage, and automated consent audit trail per CMS requirements
questions.text: Does the agent manage informed consent per JCI Standard PCC.4 and CMS 42 CFR §482.24(c) including AI-specific disclosure requirements?

questions.l1: No automated triage safety; patient prioritization is not validated against ESI criteria or clinical acuity assessment
questions.l3: Agent applies ESI-aligned triage scoring with vital sign integration, but does not implement continuous re-triage or detect clinical deterioration between assessments
questions.l5: ESI assignments are validated against a clinician-labelled sample with recorded agreement; re-triage triggers and escalation times are logged; clinicians confirm every triage level; where Annex III 5(d) applies the high-risk controls are evidenced
questions.regulatoryRef: ESI v4 Implementation Handbook; EU AI Act Annex III point 5(d)
questions.text: Does the agent implement triage safety per the Emergency Severity Index (ESI) v4 with escalation protocols, and evidence the high-risk controls where EU AI Act Annex III point 5(d) (emergency patient triage) applies?

questions.l1: No digital care coordination; care plans are fragmented across providers with no unified patient journey tracking
questions.l3: Agent maintains FHIR CarePlan resources with activity tracking, but care transitions and discharge planning are not automated or coordinated across care settings
questions.l5: Full care coordination with FHIR CarePlan lifecycle management, automated care transition notifications, discharge planning per CMS §482.43, post-discharge follow-up scheduling, readmission risk prediction, and cross-provider care plan synchronization
questions.regulatoryRef: HL7 FHIR R4 CarePlan Resource; CMS 42 CFR §482.43
questions.text: Does the agent maintain care coordination records per HL7 FHIR CarePlan resource and CMS 42 CFR §482.43 discharge planning requirements?

questions.l1: Measures are computed with unversioned or unknown logic
questions.l3: Current-year specifications are used, but inputs are not retained or the logic version is not shown
questions.l5: Each computed measure records specification version, inputs and result; reviewers can reproduce a sampled measure; specification updates are applied before the reporting year starts
questions.text: Where the agent computes clinical quality measures, does it use the CMS-published eCQM specifications for the reporting year, retain calculation inputs, and show the measure logic version to reviewers?

questions.l1: No equity assessment; diagnostic and treatment patterns are not analyzed for demographic disparities
questions.l3: Agent monitors basic demographic distribution of diagnoses and treatments, but does not perform statistical disparity analysis or implement bias mitigation
questions.l5: Comprehensive equity monitoring with statistical disparity analysis across race, ethnicity, gender, age, and socioeconomic status, automated bias detection in CDS recommendations, disparity alert system, and remediation tracking per ACA §1557
questions.text: Does the agent assess diagnostic and treatment equity across demographics per CMS 42 CFR §482.13 patient rights and ACA §1557 non-discrimination?

questions.l1: No telehealth quality standards; virtual care is delivered without standardized quality controls or regulatory compliance verification
questions.l3: Agent enforces basic telehealth quality parameters (video/audio quality, connection stability) and verifies provider licensing, but does not implement full ISO 13131 quality of service framework
questions.l5: Full telehealth quality management per ISO 13131 Clause 5 with connection quality monitoring, clinical appropriateness screening, provider licensing verification across jurisdictions, patient identity verification, and telehealth-specific informed consent management
questions.text: Does the agent implement telehealth standards per ISO 13131:2021 Clause 5 quality of service requirements and applicable state/federal telehealth regulations?

questions.l1: No medication safety automation; drug interactions and allergies are not systematically checked by the agent
questions.l3: Agent performs basic drug-drug interaction checking and allergy alerts using standard databases, but does not implement dose range checking, therapeutic duplication detection, or pharmacogenomic considerations
questions.l5: Comprehensive medication safety with multi-source interaction checking, allergy verification with cross-reactivity analysis, dose range validation, therapeutic duplication detection, pharmacogenomic integration, and closed-loop medication administration verification per JCI MMU standards
questions.text: Does the agent implement medication safety per JCI Standard MMU.1-MMU.7 including drug interaction checking and allergy verification?

questions.l1: No patient access; patients cannot view their health records or understand AI-generated clinical information through the agent
questions.l3: Agent provides patient portal access to records and basic health information, but AI-generated insights are not explained in patient-friendly language
questions.l5: Full patient access with health literacy-appropriate explanations of AI-generated insights, multilingual support, patient-reported outcome integration, shared decision-making tools, and FHIR-based Patient Access API per ONC requirements
questions.regulatoryRef: CMS 42 CFR §482.13(b)(2); ONC Patient Access API
questions.text: Does the agent provide patient-accessible health information per CMS 42 CFR §482.13(b)(2) patient rights to access medical records and ONC Patient Access API?

questions.l1: No CDI automation; clinical documentation quality is not monitored or improved by the agent
questions.l3: Agent identifies common documentation deficiencies and suggests improvements, but does not implement real-time CDI queries or track documentation quality metrics
questions.l5: Comprehensive CDI with real-time documentation quality monitoring, automated query generation for incomplete/inconsistent documentation, DRG impact analysis, physician response tracking, and documentation quality metrics per CMS §482.24 requirements
questions.regulatoryRef: CMS 42 CFR §482.24; AHIMA CDI Practice Brief
questions.text: Does the agent implement clinical documentation integrity per AHIMA CDI Practice Brief and CMS 42 CFR §482.24 medical record requirements?

questions.l1: Model updates ship with no performance monitoring or regulatory change assessment
questions.l3: Performance is monitored in aggregate, but subgroup performance and drift triggers are missing, or changes outside the PCCP are not flagged
questions.l5: Postmarket monitoring reports aggregate and subgroup performance against predefined thresholds; drift triggers open a change assessment; every change is classified as inside or outside the authorized PCCP with a record
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA AI-Enabled Device Software Functions draft guidance (January 2025); 21 U.S.C. 360e-4
questions.text: For adaptive clinical decision support that is a device, does the agent support postmarket performance monitoring across the total product life cycle, including subgroup performance and drift triggers, as recommended in FDA's AI-enabled device software functions draft guidance (January 2025), and route changes outside an authorized PCCP (21 U.S.C. 360e-4) to regulatory assessment?

questions.l1: No 510(k) evidence package; intended use or labeling or performance evidence is missing or inconsistent across agent features
questions.l3: Maintains partial 510(k) artifacts (device description, some performance evidence, draft labeling), but software documentation and testing traceability are incomplete or not audit-ready
questions.l5: Comprehensive 510(k) evidence orchestration with §807.87-aligned checklisting, software documentation (per FDA software guidance), performance or clinical evaluation evidence linkage, labeling change control, and submission-ready exports with gap reports
questions.text: Does the agent support FDA 510(k) submission evidence completeness per 21 CFR §807.87, including intended use or indications alignment, device or software description, labeling controls, and performance testing documentation for patient-facing CDS or triage functions?

questions.l1: No formal risk analysis; hazards and failure sequences are undocumented or ad-hoc
questions.l3: Maintains a risk register for major hazards, but sequences of events or foreseeable misuse and linkage to risk controls is incomplete
questions.l5: Complete §5.4 risk analysis with sequence-of-events modeling (including data quality, automation bias, handoff failures), foreseeable misuse catalog, linkage to verified risk controls, and continuous updates from post-market signals
questions.text: Does the agent perform and maintain a patient-workflow risk analysis per ISO 14971:2019 §5.4 (identify hazards, hazardous situations, foreseeable misuse, and sequences of events) for triage, CDS recommendations, care transitions, and patient communication?

questions.l1: No reconciliation workflow; medication lists are incomplete, inconsistent, or not communicated at transitions
questions.l3: Performs basic list aggregation and discrepancy flagging, but reconciliation decisions or communications are manual and inconsistently documented
questions.l5: Closed-loop reconciliation with multi-source medication history (pharmacy claims, EHR, patient report), structured discrepancy resolution, documented clinician sign-off, patient-friendly discharge med list delivery, and audit-ready reconciliation evidence
questions.text: Does the agent implement medication reconciliation across transitions of care per Joint Commission NPSG.06.01.01 (obtain or compare medication lists, resolve discrepancies, and communicate the updated list to the next provider and the patient)?

questions.l1: No GSPR evidence; risk-benefit and state-of-the-art rationale are absent for automated clinical functions
questions.l3: Documents high-level risk-benefit and some safety measures, but does not maintain state-of-the-art justification or residual risk acceptability rationale
questions.l5: Comprehensive GSPR evidence pack with state-of-the-art benchmarked controls, quantified risk-benefit support, residual risk evaluation or acceptability rationale, and continuous update from vigilance and real-world performance data
questions.text: Does the agent demonstrate EU MDR 2017/745 Annex I §1 alignment by documenting risk-benefit, state-of-the-art safety measures, and risk reduction as far as possible for patient-lifecycle automation (triage, CDS or coordination)?

questions.l1: No AI disclosure in patient interactions
questions.l3: Disclosure appears at session start only and is missing in voice or asynchronous channels
questions.l5: Disclosure appears in every channel, is stored in the transcript, and is tested per release
questions.text: Does a patient-facing agent tell natural persons they are interacting with an AI system unless that is obvious (EU AI Act Art. 50(1), applicable from 2 August 2026)?

regulatoryReferences.citation: FDA premarket notification (510(k)), 21 CFR Part 807 Subpart E
HIPAA Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules (45 CFR Parts 160 and 164)
CMS Conditions of Participation for Hospitals (42 CFR Part 482)

petition-to-law.certificationPath: L1 Basic e-petition systems → L2 Open data/FOI compliance → L3 EU EIF interoperability → L4 Full legislative AI transparency → L5 Autonomous democratic drafting support with verified inclusivity, transparency, and constitutional safeguards
petition-to-law.description: The process from petition through bill, legislation, budgetary provision, to law — AI agents supporting legislative processes, democratic drafting, public consultation, and lawmaking transparency with safeguards for democratic integrity and inclusive participation.
petition-to-law.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III (§8 covers judicial authorities and election influence, not legislative drafting); Art. 50 transparency applies
keyRisks: Exclusion of marginalized voices from AI-mediated legislative processes
Opaque AI influence on legislative drafting and law formation
Manipulation of public consultation through AI-generated submissions
Loss of democratic traceability in AI-assisted lawmaking
Algorithmic bias in petitions processed determining legislative priority
petition-to-law.name: Petition to Law

questions.l1: No legislative transparency; AI involvement in drafting, analyzing, or prioritizing legislative content is not disclosed to citizens or legislators
questions.l3: Agent documents AI roles in legislative processes and provides access logs, but does not implement EU EIF Principle 5 full transparency or SDG 16.6 accountability reporting
questions.l5: Full legislative transparency with EU EIF Principle 5 implementation, AI involvement disclosure in all legislative activities, public-accessible legislative AI register, SDG 16.6 institution effectiveness reporting, and parliamentary accountability dashboards
questions.regulatoryRef: EU EIF v2 Principle 5; UN SDG 16.6
questions.text: Does the agent implement legislative process transparency per EU EIF v2 Principle 5 (Transparency) and UN SDG 16.6 effective, accountable, and transparent institutions requirements?

questions.l1: No inclusive consultation; AI-mediated public participation favors digitally literate citizens and under-represents marginalized communities
questions.l3: Agent provides multilingual consultation and basic accessibility, but does not implement UN E-Government participation standards or OECD OG Recommendation inclusivity requirements
questions.l5: Full inclusive consultation with UN E-Government participation framework, OECD OG Art. 2 compliance, multi-channel access (digital and non-digital), minority language support, accessibility per WCAG 2.1 AA, and representativeness monitoring for consultation responses
questions.regulatoryRef: UN E-Government Survey 2024; OECD OG Rec Art. 2
questions.text: Does the agent implement public consultation inclusivity per UN E-Government Survey 2024 digital participation standards and OECD Recommendation on Open Government Article 2?

questions.l1: No open legislative data; bills, petitions, and legislative processes are not published in machine-readable open formats per EU Open Data requirements
questions.l3: Agent publishes core legislative documents in open formats, but does not implement full EU Open Data Directive compliance or INSPIRE-compliant geospatial legislative data
questions.l5: Full open data implementation with EU Open Data Directive Art. 3-5 compliance, INSPIRE-compliant geographic legislative data, legislative linked data publication, API access to legislative corpus, and reuse-friendly licensing per Creative Commons
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Open Data Directive 2019/1024 Art. 3-5; EU INSPIRE 2007/2/EC
questions.text: Does the agent implement open legislative data per EU Open Data Directive 2019/1024 Articles 3-5 and EU INSPIRE Directive for geographic legislative data with open format publication?

questions.l1: No petitioner privacy; petition systems collect and retain signatory data beyond necessity without GDPR Art. 6(1)(e) proportionality assessment
questions.l3: Agent applies GDPR lawful basis for petition processing and implements basic retention policies, but does not conduct proportionality assessments or implement Art. 9 special category protections for sensitive petition topics
questions.l5: Full petition privacy with GDPR Art. 6(1)(e) proportionality assessment, Art. 9 special category protection for sensitive petitions, minimized signatory data retention, anonymized public petition reporting, and petitioner rights fulfillment automation
questions.text: Does the agent protect petitioner privacy per GDPR Article 6(1)(e) public task basis and Article 9 for sensitive petitions involving special category data about signatories?

questions.l1: No legislative AI manipulation safeguards; petition prioritization and legislative AI tools may implement social scoring or manipulative techniques
questions.l3: Agent implements basic safeguards against biased petition processing, but does not conduct Art. 5 prohibited practice assessment for government legislative AI
questions.l5: Full Art. 5 compliance for government legislative AI with prohibited social scoring prevention, subliminal manipulation prohibition, human oversight for AI-assisted legislative drafting, and constitutional law review integration for AI-generated legislative proposals
questions.text: Does the agent prevent AI manipulation in legislative processes per EU AI Act Article 5 prohibited social scoring and subliminal manipulation prohibitions for government AI systems?

questions.l1: No legislative traceability; the connection from citizen petition through legislative stages to enacted law cannot be traced by citizens
questions.l3: Agent provides basic petition status tracking and legislative stage visibility, but does not implement end-to-end traceability or IPU Digital Parliament standard compliance
questions.l5: Full legislative traceability with petition-to-law journey visualization, amendment trail documentation, voting record integration, IPU Digital Parliament standards compliance, citizen notification of petition outcomes, and legislative impact assessment publication
questions.text: Does the agent maintain end-to-end legislative traceability from petition to enacted law per ISO 9241-210 human-centered system design and international parliamentary digital standards?

questions.l1: No access to information compliance; legislative AI systems do not support FOIA requests or proactive disclosure of legislative data
questions.l3: Agent supports basic information request processing and publishes selected legislative datasets, but does not implement full Open Data Directive 2019/1024 re-use framework or proactive disclosure program
questions.l5: Full access to information compliance with Open Data Directive 2019/1024 re-use framework, CoE CETS 205 proactive disclosure, automated FOIA response capability, legislative data quality assurance, and open license publication for all legislative documents
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Open Data Directive 2019/1024; Council of Europe Access to Information Convention (CETS 205)
questions.text: Does the agent implement FOIA/access to information compliance per the EU Open Data Directive (EU) 2019/1024 re-use of public sector information (which repealed Directive 2003/98/EC) and proactive disclosure obligations?

questions.l1: No democratic AI ethics; legislative AI deployment lacks CoE Convention Chapter III safeguards or OECD Principle 1.1 inclusive governance assessment
questions.l3: Agent implements human oversight for legislative AI decisions and basic ethics review, but does not maintain Council of Europe AI Convention Chapter III compliance or democratic legitimacy assessment
questions.l5: Full democratic AI ethics with CoE AI Convention Chapter III implementation, OECD Principle 1.1 inclusive growth assessment for legislative AI, human dignity safeguards, democratic process integrity verification, and parliamentary oversight mechanism integration
questions.regulatoryRef: CoE AI Convention 2024 Ch. III; OECD AI Principles 1.1
questions.text: Does the agent implement AI ethics in government per Council of Europe AI Convention 2024 Chapter III and OECD AI Principles 1.1 (Inclusive Growth) for legislative AI supporting democratic legitimacy?

questions.l1: No CoE Convention transparency or EU Interoperability Act compliance; AI legislative process agents lack Art. 10 transparency requirements and government AI systems are not assessed for mandatory interoperability
questions.l3: Agent implements basic transparency for AI-assisted legislative activities, but does not address CoE Convention Art. 10 specific oversight requirements or EU Interoperability Act mandatory assessment for government AI
questions.l5: Full CoE AI Convention Art. 10 transparency with legislative AI oversight mechanisms, EU Interoperability Act mandatory interoperability assessment, cross-border legislative data exchange capability, and transparent AI governance reporting to parliamentary oversight bodies
questions.regulatoryRef: CoE AI Convention Art. 10; EU Interoperability Act 2024
questions.text: Does the agent implement Council of Europe AI Convention 2024 Article 10 transparency and oversight requirements for AI in legislative processes and EU Interoperability Act 2024 mandatory interoperability assessment for government AI systems?

questions.l1: No Art. 5 implementation: data is not machine-readable, lacks metadata, and provides no API or bulk access for reuse
questions.l3: Some open formats/feeds exist, but metadata, API or bulk access, update SLAs, and compliance evidence are incomplete
questions.l5: Full Art. 5 compliance with machine-readable releases, metadata completeness, API and bulk access for dynamic datasets, publication and update SLAs, and audit-ready evidence artifacts
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Open Data Directive (EU) 2019/1024 Article 5 by ensuring legislative/petition documents and datasets are made available (1) in machine-readable formats, (2) with complete metadata, (3) with bulk download and where data is dynamic API access, (4) with publication and update SLAs, and (5) with evidence artifacts (metadata schema, API docs, change logs, uptime metrics) to demonstrate ongoing compliance?

questions.l1: No INSPIRE interoperability: geospatial legislative data is ad hoc and cannot be harmonised or validated against INSPIRE implementing rules
questions.l3: Some geospatial data is published, but schema harmonisation, conformance validation, and evidence reports are incomplete
questions.l5: Full Art. 7 interoperability with INSPIRE-aligned models, automated conformance validation, documented transformations, and published conformance reports suitable for oversight
questions.text: For any geospatial legislative datasets (affected regions, constituency maps, project locations, zoning overlays), does the agent implement INSPIRE Directive 2007/2/EC Article 7 interoperability by aligning datasets and services to INSPIRE implementing rules (harmonised data models, schemas, code lists), validating conformance, and publishing conformance reports and transformation pipelines as evidence?

questions.l1: No SQuaRE quality measurement: datasets lack defined quality measures, dashboards, or remediation evidence
questions.l3: Some quality checks exist, but measures are incomplete, not tied to §2512, or not published with evidence of remediation
questions.l5: Full §2512 operationalization with defined quality measures, automated measurement, published quality reports per release, defect/remediation tracking, and audit-ready evidence bundles
questions.text: Does the agent implement ISO 25000 SQuaRE §2512 by defining a data and system quality model for petition-to-law datasets (e.g., completeness, accuracy, timeliness, consistency, provenance), computing quality measures, publishing quality dashboards/reports with each release, and retaining audit evidence (measurement definitions, sampling, defect logs, remediation actions)?

questions.l1: No UN EGov 2022 mapping: participation features are ad hoc and not benchmarkable against 2022 criteria
questions.l3: Some participation measures exist, but mapping to UN EGov 2022 components and benchmarking metrics is incomplete
questions.l5: Full UN EGov Survey 2022 alignment with mapped participation services, accessibility and inclusion controls, representativeness monitoring, and published benchmark-ready metrics
questions.text: Does the agent implement inclusive public consultation and e-participation in a way that is explicitly mapped to the UN E-Government Survey 2022 e-participation framework (e-information, e-consultation, e-decision-making), including multi-channel participation, accessibility, representativeness monitoring, and published participation metrics suitable for annual benchmarking?

questions.l1: No citation governance: references drift and anchors are inconsistent across artifacts
questions.l3: Some mapping exists but is manual and inconsistently applied
questions.l5: Versioned mapping with periodic review and automated consistency checks ensuring audit-defensible statutory anchors
questions.text: Does the program maintain a versioned control-to-citation map for PSI/Open Data and access-to-information obligations (e.g., mapping any legacy 2003/98 references to 2019/1024 where required), with periodic review and automated checks to keep statutory anchors consistent across questions, datasets, and evidence exports?

questions.l1: AI-generated public texts are published without disclosure
questions.l3: Disclosure is applied to some channels, and the human-review exception is claimed without records
questions.l5: Every published AI-generated text carries a disclosure, or a record shows the human reviewer and the editor responsible, checked before publication
questions.text: When the agent generates or manipulates text published to inform the public on legislative or petition matters, does the deployer disclose that the text was artificially generated or manipulated, as EU AI Act Article 50(4) requires unless the text underwent human review with editorial responsibility?

sdgAlignment: SDG 16 — Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions

privacy-security-mobility.certificationPath: L1 Basic privacy controls → L2 GDPR/CCPA baseline compliance → L3 ISO 27701 certified privacy management → L4 Full ETSI/UNECE cybersecurity compliance → L5 Autonomous zero-trust privacy-preserving AI with continuous compliance verification
privacy-security-mobility.description: Last-mile privacy and security through network and communications — AI agents protecting end-user privacy and security in local and wide-area networks, IoT ecosystems, connected vehicles, and smart infrastructure with emphasis on data protection, cybersecurity resilience, and zero-trust architecture.
privacy-security-mobility.euAIActClassification: Annex III §1 — biometrics (remote biometric identification, biometric categorisation, emotion recognition) where used; §6 only for law-enforcement use
keyRisks: Mass surveillance enablement through AI-optimized monitoring
Personal data exfiltration through compromised IoT devices
Vehicle cybersecurity attack enabling physical harm per UNECE R155
Privacy erosion from algorithmic profiling without consent
Security theater through compliance-only approach lacking real protection
privacy-security-mobility.name: Privacy & Security

questions.l1: No privacy by design; data collection is maximalist with no systematic minimization, pseudonymisation, or purpose limitation controls
questions.l3: Agent implements data minimization for primary data flows and pseudonymises stored data, but does not systematically enforce purpose limitation or automate privacy impact assessment
questions.l5: Minimisation and pseudonymisation are enforced in configuration for every processing activity, purpose limitation is enforced technically, a DPIA exists for each high-risk processing operation, and the controls are mapped to ISO/IEC 27701:2025.
questions.text: Does the agent implement data protection by design per GDPR Article 25 including data minimization, pseudonymisation, and purpose limitation in all data processing activities?

questions.l1: No vehicle cybersecurity management; connected vehicle AI does not implement CSMS or systematic threat analysis and risk assessment
questions.l3: Agent implements vehicle cybersecurity controls and basic TARA, but does not maintain full UNECE R155 §7 CSMS documentation or continuous threat monitoring
questions.l5: Full UNECE R155 CSMS with continuous TARA per ISO 21434 §8, cybersecurity event detection and response, OTA security update governance, incident escalation, and complete CSMS documentation for type approval
questions.text: Does the agent implement vehicle cybersecurity per UNECE WP.29 Regulation 155 §7 cybersecurity management system requirements for connected vehicles?

questions.l1: Devices ship or reset to shared default credentials, lack an update mechanism, or there is no disclosure policy.
questions.l3: Credentials are unique for most devices and updates are supported, but reset behaviour, update integrity or the disclosure process is not evidenced fleet-wide.
questions.l5: A fleet-wide test shows no universal default credentials (including after reset), updates are integrity-checked, the disclosure policy is published, and each baseline provision maps to evidence.
questions.text: Does the agent enforce the consumer-IoT baseline of ETSI EN 303 645 V3.1.3 for the devices it manages, including no universal default passwords (unique per-device or user-set credentials, also after reset), secure software updates and a vulnerability disclosure policy?

questions.l1: No zero-trust principles; network access uses perimeter-based trust with no microsegmentation or continuous verification
questions.l3: Agent implements identity-based access controls and some microsegmentation, but does not fully apply zero-trust principles across all network communications
questions.l5: Full zero-trust architecture with microsegmentation per NIST SP 800-207, continuous device/user/workload verification, least privilege enforcement, encrypted east-west traffic, and zero-trust maturity assessment
questions.text: Does the agent implement zero-trust architecture per NIST SP 800-207 principles including microsegmentation, least privilege access, and continuous verification?

questions.l1: No formal incident response; incidents are handled ad hoc without containment or records.
questions.l3: Incidents are detected, logged and contained, but analysis, stakeholder reporting or mitigation records are incomplete.
questions.l5: Each incident has a record covering management, analysis, communication and mitigation, forensic evidence is preserved, and lessons learned are fed back into controls with a recorded change.
questions.text: Does the agent support cybersecurity incident response per the NIST CSF 2.0 Respond (RS) function: incident management, incident analysis, response reporting and communication, and incident mitigation?

questions.l1: No consumer rights fulfillment; privacy notices are static and data subject/consumer rights cannot be exercised digitally
questions.l3: Agent provides privacy notices per GDPR Art. 13-14, but does not automate rights fulfillment or track response deadlines
questions.l5: Full rights management with automated DSAR processing, consent withdrawal enforcement, GDPR 30-day and CCPA 45-day response tracking, portability export generation, and transparent privacy notice management with version control
questions.text: Does the agent implement privacy transparency per GDPR Articles 13-14 information obligations and CCPA §1798.100 consumer rights with automated rights fulfillment?

questions.l1: CRA applied or ignored with no recorded scope decision; components not inventoried.
questions.l3: Scope is recorded and an SBOM exists, but vulnerability handling or secure-development evidence is incomplete.
questions.l5: A scope decision is recorded per product, SSDF practices are evidenced in the pipeline, the SBOM is maintained per release, vulnerability handling runs to documented timelines, and the Art. 32 conformity route is documented.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU CRA Art. 2(2)(c), 2(4); EU CRA Art. 13; NIST SP 800-218
questions.text: For products with digital elements in CRA scope (type-approved vehicles under Regulation (EU) 2019/2144 and marine equipment under Directive 2014/90/EU are excluded, Art. 2(2)(c) and 2(4)), does the agent's software supply chain meet the CRA Art. 13 manufacturer obligations (security by design, vulnerability handling, software bill of materials) using NIST SP 800-218 SSDF practices, ahead of general application on 11 December 2027?

questions.l1: No obligation register.
questions.l3: A register exists but is not versioned or not linked to controls.
questions.l5: The register is versioned, each enforced control cites the obligation it implements, and a register change triggers a control review with a recorded decision.
questions.text: Does the agent maintain a versioned obligation register (GDPR, UNECE R155/R156, ETSI EN 303 645, NIS2) that is bound to its control configuration, so that each enforced control cites the obligation it implements?

questions.l1: No TARA; threats and treatment decisions are not documented.
questions.l3: A TARA exists, but attack-path analysis, traceability to cybersecurity goals, or change-triggered review is incomplete.
questions.l5: Each item has a versioned TARA with all listed artefacts, traceability to goals and requirements, and a recorded re-assessment after each relevant change or incident.
questions.text: Does the agent produce and maintain item-level threat analysis and risk assessment (TARA) per ISO/SAE 21434:2021 (TARA methods, Clause 15): asset identification, threat scenarios, attack paths, impact and feasibility ratings, risk determination and treatment decisions, traced to cybersecurity goals and re-run on change or incident?

questions.l1: No §7.3.3 loop: monitoring is ad hoc, corrective actions are not evidenced, and CSMS effectiveness cannot be demonstrated for audit and type approval
questions.l3: Monitoring and response exist but evidence, effectiveness verification, and audit ready CSMS records are incomplete or inconsistently maintained
questions.l5: Full §7.3.3 compliance with continuous monitoring, governed escalation, corrective action and effectiveness verification, and maintained CSMS evidence packs supporting type approval and surveillance audits
questions.text: Does the agent implement UNECE WP.29 R155 §7.3.3 by operating a CSMS effectiveness and post development monitoring loop, including (1) continuous monitoring for vulnerabilities and cyber events across fleet and backend and supply chain, (2) defined escalation and decision criteria, (3) evidence of corrective actions and verification of effectiveness, and (4) audit ready CSMS records demonstrating ongoing compliance for type approval and surveillance audits?

questions.l1: Vehicle and passenger data is processed without documented security measures
questions.l3: Encryption is in place, but restoration and regular testing are not evidenced
questions.l5: Each Article 32(1) measure mapped to controls with test evidence, restoration exercised on a schedule, and measures reviewed when risk changes
questions.text: Does the agent apply the security of processing measures in GDPR Article 32(1) to vehicle and passenger data: pseudonymisation and encryption, ongoing confidentiality, integrity and availability, timely restoration after an incident, and regular testing of the measures?

questions.l1: No reporting clock for exploited vulnerabilities or severe incidents.
questions.l3: Events are timestamped and a contact exists, but the 24-hour, 72-hour and final-report deadlines are tracked by hand.
questions.l5: Each event is classified, all three submissions are drafted from evidence and tracked to submission with timestamps, and a reporting drill is on record.

questions.l3: Agent calculates key performance indicators per ISO 24510 (service quality, reliability, customer satisfaction) but does not benchmark against peer utilities or identify improvement priorities
questions.l5: Full performance benchmarking with ISO 24510 indicator calculation, peer utility comparison, trend analysis, improvement priority identification, customer satisfaction integration, and transparent public reporting of service performance
questions.text: Does the agent support water service performance benchmarking per ISO 24510:2007 service assessment guidelines?

questions.l1: No OT cybersecurity; water treatment SCADA systems are not protected by AI-managed security controls
questions.l3: Agent monitors SCADA network traffic for anomalies and enforces access controls per NIST SP 800-82, but incident response and recovery for OT systems is not automated
questions.l5: OT network monitoring covers the SCADA systems the agent touches, IT/OT segmentation and access controls are enforced and tested, and OT incident response for agent-touched systems is exercised with results recorded
questions.text: Does the agent implement SCADA/ICS cybersecurity for water infrastructure per NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (OT network monitoring, IT/OT segmentation and access control)?

questions.l1: No PFAS parameter logic
questions.l3: PFAS results are checked against the parametric values, but analytical-method performance is not validated and exceedance follow-up is manual
questions.l5: PFAS results carry validated analytical-method data, exceedances trigger recorded remedial measures and public-information decisions, and monitoring results are reported to the competent authority from the same records
questions.regulatoryRef: Directive (EU) 2020/2184 Annex I Part B (PFAS Total, Sum of PFAS)
questions.text: Does the agent monitor the PFAS parameters in Annex I Part B of Directive (EU) 2020/2184 (PFAS Total and/or Sum of PFAS), applicable since 12 Jan 2026, with exceedance alerts, remedial-action records and reporting of results to the competent authority?

questions.l1: PFAS limits are hard-coded with no regulatory-state tracking
questions.l3: PFOA/PFOS limits are applied and the other limits are flagged as proposed for rescission, but effective dates are not versioned
questions.l5: Each PFAS limit carries its legal status and effective date, rule changes are applied when final with the change logged, and monitoring and reporting continue under the rule in force
questions.regulatoryRef: 40 CFR Part 141 Subpart Z (PFAS NPDWR, April 2024)
questions.text: Does the agent track the current US PFAS drinking-water regulatory state (the April 2024 NPDWR in 40 CFR Part 141 Subpart Z, plus EPA's two 20 May 2026 proposed rules: exemptions extending PFOA/PFOS MCL compliance from 26 Apr 2029 to 26 Apr 2031, and rescission of the PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA and mixture determinations) and apply only the requirements in force?

questions.l1: No risk assessment/risk management workflow; compliance relies on periodic testing without a documented risk-based assessment or managed control measures
questions.l3: Maintains a documented risk assessment and some risk management actions, but updates are periodic/manual and control verification evidence is incomplete or not audit-ready
questions.l5: Each stage has a documented, dated risk assessment and risk-management measures with verification evidence, reviews are triggered by change and by schedule, and an evidence pack for competent-authority review is generated from the same records
questions.regulatoryRef: Directive (EU) 2020/2184 (risk-based approach: catchment, supply system, domestic distribution)
questions.text: Does the agent support and evidence the Directive (EU) 2020/2184 risk-based approach — risk assessment and risk management of catchment areas (due July 2027) and of the supply system and domestic distribution (due January 2029) — including documentation, review frequency and control verification?

questions.l1: No BSAP alignment; discharges and measures are not linked to BSAP objectives/targets and reporting is absent
questions.l3: Tracks some nutrient/chemical indicators and reports periodically, but does not attribute loads, manage measures against targets, or demonstrate measure effectiveness over time
questions.l5: Full BSAP-aligned governance with load attribution modeling, measure selection and effectiveness tracking, cross-border reporting-ready outputs, and continuous improvement loops tied to BSAP objectives
questions.text: Does the agent implement monitoring, decision controls, and reporting aligned to HELCOM Baltic Sea Action Plan (BSAP) commitments relevant to its operations (e.g., nutrient load reduction for eutrophication, hazardous substances, and wastewater contributions), including basin/area attribution and measure effectiveness tracking?

questions.l1: No WSP implementation; elements are missing (system assessment, monitoring, procedures, verification) and documentation is not controlled
questions.l3: Implements most WSP components with documented procedures and some verification, but operational monitoring and periodic review are incomplete or not consistently evidenced
questions.l5: Comprehensive WSP implementation with continuous operational monitoring, automated verification and review cycles, incident/normal SOP enforcement, controlled documentation, and audit-ready evidence mapped to §4.1 elements
questions.text: Does the agent ensure Water Safety Plan implementation consistent with WHO GDWQ (4th ed.) §4.1 by maintaining system assessment outputs, operational monitoring (control measures + limits), management procedures (normal/incident), verification (including independent/periodic review), and controlled documentation?

questions.l1: No equipment conformity/readiness checks; compliance relies on manual logs and discharge assertions
questions.l3: Tracks equipment certificates and maintenance logs, but does not detect bypass/malfunction patterns or reconcile operational readiness with discharge events
questions.l5: Integrated compliance with certificate validation, maintenance/condition monitoring, bypass anomaly detection, and evidence linkage to each discharge decision/event
questions.regulatoryRef: MARPOL Annex IV Reg. 11 (+ equipment approval/operation)
questions.text: Does the agent verify vessel sewage system conformity and operational readiness (approved equipment status, maintenance/inspection records, alarms/bypass detection) alongside MARPOL Annex IV Reg. 11 discharge-condition monitoring?

questions.l1: Agent decisions use ad hoc data with no link to the statutory monitoring programmes
questions.l3: Agent ingests monitoring programme data but does not track coverage gaps or which programme each record belongs to
questions.l5: Each decision cites the monitoring programme, station and sampling date it relied on, coverage gaps per water body are flagged, and decisions on under-monitored bodies are escalated for review
questions.text: Does the agent feed water-quality decisions from monitoring data that follow the Water Framework Directive 2000/60/EC Article 8 surveillance, operational and investigative monitoring programmes (Annex V), and flag water bodies whose monitoring coverage is incomplete?

questions.l1: The agent and the systems it operates are outside the RRA and ERP
questions.l3: The agent is listed in the RRA and the ERP names a manual fallback, but agent failure and compromise scenarios are not assessed
questions.l5: Agent failure and compromise scenarios are assessed in the RRA, the ERP fallback is exercised with results recorded, and RRA/ERP certification dates for the system's population band are tracked
questions.text: For US community water systems serving more than 3,300 people, does the agent support the SDWA Section 1433 risk and resilience assessment (including the electronic, computer or other automated systems it operates and their security) and the emergency response plan's cybersecurity strategies, with certification dates tracked?

questions.l1: No determination whether the agent is a safety component in water supply
questions.l3: Classification documented and dosing/pressure actions logged, but override, stop and fail-safe are untested
questions.l5: Classification recorded with reasoning, Art. 12 logs retained and protected from alteration, override/stop and fail-safe exercised in drills with results recorded, and the evidence pack dated against 2 Dec 2027
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Annex III point 2, Art. 12, Art. 14(4)(d)-(e), Art. 15(4)
questions.text: Where the agent is a safety component in drinking-water supply (e.g. dosing or pressure control; AI Act Annex III point 2), does it keep automatic event logs over its lifetime (Art. 12), give operators override and a stop to a safe state (Art. 14(4)(d)-(e)), and have a backup or fail-safe plan (Art. 15(4)), ready for the 2 Dec 2027 application date?

questions.l1: Agent vendors are outside the NIS2 risk-management measures and agent incidents have no reporting path
questions.l3: Agent vendors are in the supplier register with security requirements, but incident reporting on the NIS2 timeline is not rehearsed
questions.l5: Supply-chain security covers agent vendors with evidence, and significant-incident reporting is rehearsed against the 24h early warning / 72h notification / one-month final report timeline with timings recorded
questions.regulatoryRef: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2) Annex I drinking water and waste water sectors, Art. 21, Art. 23
questions.text: Where the operator is an essential entity in the drinking water or waste water sector, do its NIS2 cybersecurity risk-management measures cover the agent's vendors, and can a significant incident involving the agent be reported on the 24h early warning / 72h notification / one-month final report timeline?

skills-training.certificationPath: L1 Basic training delivery → L2 Competency-based assessment with standards alignment → L3 Full EQF/NQF compliant AI-assisted training → L4 Industry-integrated adaptive skills development → L5 Autonomous vocational training governance with verified employment outcomes
skills-training.description: Occupational skills including trades, crafts, and vocational education — covering AI in skills development, competency assessment, and workforce readiness with emphasis on practical skill validation, industry alignment, and equitable access to training.
skills-training.euAIActClassification: Annex III §3 — education and vocational training; §4(a) where used for recruitment or selection
keyRisks: Skills assessment bias disadvantaging non-traditional learners
Practical competency gaps from over-reliance on AI simulation
Industry misalignment from AI-generated curriculum without employer input
Credential fraud through AI-manipulated competency evidence
Digital divide excluding trade workers from AI-enhanced training
skills-training.name: Skills & Vocational Training

questions.l1: No EQF alignment; competency assessments do not map to recognized qualification framework levels
questions.l3: Agent maps training outcomes to EQF level descriptors, but does not validate assessment rigor against NQF requirements or support cross-border qualification recognition
questions.l5: Full EQF/NQF alignment with competency mapping to level descriptors, assessment rigor validation, cross-border recognition support, micro-credential EQF leveling, and automated qualification comparison per Council Recommendation
questions.text: Does the agent align competency assessment with EQF level descriptors per Council Recommendation 2017/C 189/03 and national qualifications framework requirements?

questions.l1: No practical competency safeguards; AI-based assessment may certify practical skills without adequate hands-on verification
questions.l3: Agent distinguishes between theoretical and practical competencies and requires hands-on assessment for safety-critical skills, but does not implement comprehensive practical validation frameworks
questions.l5: Full practical competency validation with hands-on assessment requirements for safety-critical skills, simulation-to-practice transfer verification, workplace assessment integration, competency evidence portfolios, and practical skill decay monitoring
questions.text: Does the agent implement practical competency validation per the UNESCO TVET Strategy and ensure AI simulation does not replace essential hands-on assessment?

questions.l1: No equity assessment; AI-driven career guidance may channel disadvantaged learners into lower-value pathways
questions.l3: Agent monitors training access by demographic group and flags underrepresentation, but does not assess career pathway equity or prevent algorithmic tracking
questions.l5: Comprehensive equity with demographic access monitoring, career pathway equity analysis, anti-tracking safeguards, financial barrier identification, accessibility accommodation, and transparent pathway recommendation methodology per UNESCO TVET strategy
questions.text: Does the agent ensure equitable access to vocational training per UNESCO TVET Strategy and prevent AI-driven tracking that limits career pathways?

questions.l1: No management system covers AI-delivered or AI-assessed courses
questions.l3: A quality management system exists, but AI components are outside its scope or not covered by internal audit
questions.l5: The ISO 21001-aligned management system scope names AI-delivered and AI-assessed learning; design reviews, learner feedback and internal audit records cover AI components; nonconformities are tracked to closure
questions.text: Does the training provider run an educational organization management system aligned to ISO 21001 whose scope includes AI-delivered and AI-assessed learning — design, delivery, assessment, learner feedback and internal audit?

questions.l1: No credential transparency; AI-assessed competencies are not documented in verifiable, employer-readable formats
questions.l3: Agent generates digital credentials with basic competency descriptions, but does not implement full Europass DCI or support automated employer verification
questions.l5: Full credential transparency with Europass DCI integration, verifiable competency evidence, employer verification APIs, competency-to-job-requirement mapping, and transparent AI assessment methodology documentation
questions.text: Does the agent provide credential transparency per Europass Digital Credentials Infrastructure and support employer verification of AI-assessed competencies?

questions.l1: No safety training compliance; AI-delivered occupational safety training is not validated against regulatory requirements
questions.l3: Agent delivers safety training content aligned with OSHA requirements, but does not verify comprehension or track certification currency
questions.l5: Full safety training compliance with regulatory content validation, comprehension verification, certification tracking, refresher scheduling, incident-triggered retraining, and competency evidence documentation per OSHA requirements
questions.text: Does the agent implement workplace safety training compliance per OSHA 29 CFR §1910.132?

questions.l1: No data lifecycle management; learner records are retained indefinitely without erasure capability or retention policy
questions.l3: Agent supports basic data deletion requests, but does not balance GDPR erasure rights with qualification record retention obligations
questions.l5: Full data lifecycle management with GDPR Art. 17 erasure processing, retention policy automation balancing erasure rights with qualification record obligations, anonymization for expired records, and transparent data retention documentation
questions.text: Does the agent maintain learner progress records per GDPR Article 17 right to erasure balanced with qualification record retention requirements?

questions.l1: No RPL support; AI assessment only recognizes formal learning credentials and disadvantages experienced workers without formal qualifications
questions.l3: Agent accepts portfolio-based evidence for RPL, but AI assessment may undervalue non-formal learning or apply formal assessment criteria inappropriately
questions.l5: Comprehensive RPL with portfolio assessment, work experience validation, non-formal learning recognition, cultural competency consideration, flexible evidence acceptance, and equitable assessment criteria per UNESCO RPL guidelines
questions.text: Does the agent support recognition of prior learning (RPL) per UNESCO Guidelines on RPL and prevent AI assessment bias against non-formal/informal learning?

questions.l1: No ADA Title II controls: learner flows are inaccessible and there is no structured reasonable modification or auxiliary aid support for training or assessments
questions.l3: Provides some accessibility features and an accommodation request channel, but modifications and auxiliary aids and alternative assessment pathways are inconsistent or not auditable
questions.l5: End to end ADA Title II readiness with WCAG aligned accessible UX, auxiliary aid support, documented reasonable modification workflows, alternative assessment routing, and auditable accommodation decisions and outcomes for training and assessment
questions.text: If used by (or on behalf of) a public entity VET provider, does the agent ensure ADA Title II §12132 compliance by providing equal access and reasonable modifications and auxiliary aids for learners with disabilities across (1) program access and admissions, (2) learning delivery, and (3) competency assessment (including alternative assessment formats and human review where needed)?

questions.l1: No training leave support: participation assumes learners can attend and there are no workflows for leave entitlement, scheduling constraints, or documentation
questions.l3: Provides basic scheduling and attendance tracking, but leave entitlements and non retaliation and audit ready documentation are incomplete
questions.l5: Full training leave operationalization with entitlement rule configuration, leave request routing, non retaliation controls, documentation templates, and audit logs linking leave approvals to training participation and outcomes
questions.text: Does the agent support ILO R195 §7 by enabling compliant training leave management (eligibility rules, leave requests and scheduling, non retaliation safeguards, documentation for employers and authorities, and equitable access for non standard workers), including audit ready records of leave decisions and participation outcomes?

questions.l1: No UNESCO 2022 §4.2 operationalization: there is no defined quality and inclusion enablers loop or evidence reporting
questions.l3: Tracks some indicators (completion, satisfaction) and has informal partner inputs, but enablers and inclusion mechanisms are partial and not evidence grade
questions.l5: Full UNESCO 2022 §4.2 operationalization with defined QA indicators, instructor capability supports, employer and work based learning integration, inclusion supports, and auditable evidence reporting tied to continuous improvement actions
questions.text: Does the agent operationalize UNESCO TVET 2022 §4.2 by implementing a TVET quality and inclusion enablers loop (e.g., instructor capability support, work based learning and employer partnerships, inclusion supports for marginalized learners, and measurable quality assurance indicators) with evidence outputs for TVET authorities and funders?

questions.l1: Learning services are generated or delivered with no recorded needs analysis
questions.l3: Needs are captured informally and are not linked to learning goals or evaluation criteria
questions.l5: A recorded needs analysis per service, with sponsor sign-off, traced to learning goals and evaluation criteria and revisited when evaluation shows a gap
questions.text: Before an AI-delivered learning service is designed, does the provider record a learning-needs analysis — learner prerequisites and constraints, sponsor or employer requirements, accessibility and adjustment needs — and use it to set the learning goals and evaluation criteria, aligned to ISO 29993:2017 (learning services outside formal education)?

questions.l1: No contestation: AI driven placement and assessment outcomes are not explainable and cannot be appealed
questions.l3: Provides basic explanations and a manual appeal email address, but evidence review and human reconsideration SLAs are undefined
questions.l5: Full oversight and contestability with reason codes, evidence bundles, defined appeal workflow and SLAs, and auditable human reconsideration outcomes
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 14; EU AI Act Annex III §3(a)
questions.text: For AI influenced vocational training access, placement, or competency assessment decisions, does the agent provide meaningful human oversight and a learner contestation and appeal pathway (clear reasons, evidence review, and timely human reconsideration), consistent with high risk controls expected for Annex III §3(a) systems?

questions.l1: Learners are not told that AI proctoring is used, and flags lead directly to sanctions
questions.l3: Learners are notified, but flags are not consistently reviewed by a person before a sanction
questions.l5: Notice before each assessment, every flag reviewed by a trained person with the evidence shown, sanction decisions logged with reasons, and a route for the learner to contest
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Annex III §3(d); EU AI Act Art. 26(11)
questions.text: Where the agent monitors or detects prohibited behaviour of learners during tests (EU AI Act Annex III point 3(d)), does the deployer inform each learner that a high-risk AI system is being used, as Article 26(11) requires, and route every flag to a human reviewer before any sanction?

questions.l1: No notice, explanation, correction or human-review path
questions.l3: Notice exists; adverse-outcome descriptions and human review are manual and untracked
questions.l5: Automated notice at interaction; adverse-outcome descriptions issued within 30 days; tracked correction and human-reconsideration requests; records kept at least 3 years
questions.text: Where the agent is used in decisions about access to or eligibility for education or training for Colorado consumers, does the deployer support the Colorado SB26-189 deployer duties (act signed 2026-05-14; developer documentation duties from 2027-01-01): notice at the point of interaction, a plain-language description of the technology's role within 30 days after an adverse outcome, correction of factually inaccurate personal data, meaningful human reconsideration on request, and records kept at least 3 years?

source-to-sustenance.certificationPath: L1 Basic species identification → L2 Habitat monitoring with CITES compliance → L3 Ecosystem-level biodiversity assessment per CBD → L4 Predictive conservation with REDD+ integration → L5 Autonomous ecological governance with verified biodiversity net gain

complianceFrameworkRefs.label: FAO Code of Conduct for Responsible Fisheries

complianceFrameworks: FAO Code of Conduct for Responsible Fisheries
source-to-sustenance.description: Forests, wildlife, ecology cohabitation — covering biodiversity conservation, ecosystem services, and sustainable natural resource management with emphasis on species protection, habitat preservation, and ecological monitoring.
source-to-sustenance.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III; high-risk only under Art. 6(1) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a product covered by Annex I legislation — otherwise Art. 4 (AI literacy), Art. 5 (prohibited practices) and Art. 50 (transparency) apply
keyRisks: Species misidentification leading to illegal trade facilitation
Habitat destruction undetected by remote sensing AI
Biodiversity offset fraud through manipulated ecological assessments
Indigenous community displacement from AI-optimized conservation zones
Invasive species introduction through AI-managed translocation programs
source-to-sustenance.name: Source to Sustenance

questions.l1: Trade decisions are made without appendix checks or permit validation
questions.l3: Appendix listing is checked and permit fields validated, but authority checks are spot checks and identification relies on unrecorded manual input
questions.l5: Every trade record carries the appendix check (list version date), permit validation result incl. authority confirmation, identification method and evidence, and a hold decision; failed or incomplete checks block the trade
questions.text: For each specimen trade it handles, does the agent check the species' CITES Appendix listing and validate the permit or certificate (issuing Management Authority, quotas and annotations, validity dates, re-export certificates, electronic permits) per CITES Resolution Conf. 12.3 (Rev. CoP20)?

questions.l1: No biodiversity monitoring; ecological health indicators are not tracked or reported
questions.l3: Agent tracks basic biodiversity metrics (species counts, habitat area) against 30x30 targets, but lacks ecosystem-level health assessment and trend analysis
questions.l5: Indicators have documented baselines, methods and uncertainty, remote-sensing inputs are versioned, and reports map each indicator to GBF Target 3
questions.text: Does the agent monitor biodiversity indicators for the sites it manages and report them against Kunming-Montreal GBF Target 3?

questions.l1: No forest product traceability; timber and non-timber forest product origins are not verified
questions.l3: Agent tracks chain-of-custody certificates and validates chain-of-custody claims, but gaps exist at processing and conversion stages
questions.l5: Mass balance and conversion factors are reconciled at every processing step, certificates are validated against the certification body database, mixed-source percentages are recomputed, and mismatches block the claim
questions.text: Does the agent maintain forest product chain of custody per the PEFC ST 2002:2020 chain of custody requirements?

questions.l1: No REDD+ safeguard implementation; carbon offset projects do not verify indigenous rights or environmental integrity
questions.l3: Agent tracks FPIC documentation and basic safeguard compliance for REDD+ projects, but does not independently verify community consent or monitor ongoing safeguard adherence
questions.l5: Full Cancun Safeguard implementation with FPIC verification protocols, indigenous knowledge integration, benefit-sharing transparency, biodiversity co-benefit monitoring, and independent grievance mechanism integration
questions.regulatoryRef: UNFCCC Decision 1/CP.16 Appendix I — Cancun Safeguards
questions.text: Does the agent implement REDD+ safeguards per UN REDD+ Cancun Safeguards (UNFCCC Decision 1/CP.16 Appendix I) including free, prior, and informed consent (FPIC)?

questions.l1: No wetland-specific monitoring; Ramsar site obligations are not tracked or managed
questions.l3: Agent monitors basic wetland parameters (water level, area) for designated Ramsar sites, but does not assess ecological character change or implement wise use principles
questions.l5: Comprehensive Ramsar site management with ecological character description monitoring, early warning of adverse change per Art. 3.2, wise use implementation tracking, and automated reporting to national Ramsar committees
questions.text: Does the agent manage wetland conservation obligations per Ramsar Convention Article 3.1 including ecological character monitoring and wise use principles?

questions.l1: No EIA integration; development decisions do not include automated biodiversity impact assessment
questions.l3: Agent generates biodiversity impact sections for EIAs with species and habitat data, but impact quantification relies on generic models rather than site-specific ecological data
questions.l5: Full EIA biodiversity integration with site-specific ecological surveys, cumulative impact modeling, mitigation hierarchy application (avoid-minimize-restore-offset), biodiversity net gain calculation, and long-term monitoring plan generation
questions.text: Does the agent support environmental impact assessment per EU EIA Directive 2011/92/EU Article 5 with biodiversity-specific impact quantification?

questions.l1: No invasive species screening; translocation and trade decisions do not assess invasion risk
questions.l3: Agent screens species against EU IAS list of Union concern and national lists, but does not perform pathway-level risk assessment or early detection monitoring
questions.l5: Each translocation or trade decision involving a non-native species records a risk assessment covering the elements Article 5 requires, checked against the Union list and national lists, and the assessment is retained with the decision
questions.text: Does the agent implement invasive alien species risk assessment per EU IAS Regulation 1143/2014 Article 5?

questions.l1: DSI use is not recorded and no contribution assessment exists
questions.l3: DSI use and provenance are recorded for some datasets; the threshold assessment is ad hoc
questions.l5: Every DSI dataset used commercially has provenance recorded, the annual threshold assessment (assets, sales, profit) is documented, and the contribution decision and any Cali Fund certificate are retained
questions.text: Where the agent uses digital sequence information on genetic resources in commercial activity, does it record DSI provenance (country of origin where known) and assess whether the operator exceeds the CBD Decision 16/2 thresholds at which a Cali Fund contribution is expected (indicative 1% of profits or 0.1% of revenue)?

questions.l1: Traditional knowledge is collected/used without community approval, without protection of sensitive knowledge, and without benefit-sharing or community involvement in decisions
questions.l3: Community approval/involvement is documented for some uses and sensitive knowledge is partially protected, but governance rules and benefit-sharing are inconsistent and not auditable
questions.l5: End-to-end 8(j) compliance: community-defined governance rules enforced (including confidentiality/sacred knowledge controls), documented approval & involvement for each use-case, ongoing co-management participation, and transparent benefit-sharing reporting with grievance redress
questions.text: Does the agent ensure approval and involvement of indigenous and local communities and protect traditional knowledge used in biodiversity decision-making, including documented community governance rules and equitable benefit-sharing, per CBD Article 8(j)?

questions.l1: No catch certificates are collected/verified; fishery product legality is not evidenced and imports rely on unverified supplier claims
questions.l3: Catch certificates are submitted through CATCH and spot-checked, but vessel/area/species mismatches and downstream transformations are not consistently reconciled
questions.l5: Every consignment's catch certificate is submitted and checked in CATCH, vessel, flag-state, species and area fields are validated, chain of custody is reconciled through processing and transshipment, and evidence is exportable per consignment
questions.regulatoryRef: Council Regulation (EC) No 1005/2008 Art. 12, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/2842 (CATCH)
questions.text: Does the agent verify and retain EU IUU catch certificates for fishery products (including validation of flag state information, vessel identity, species/FAO area, quantities, and chain-of-custody consistency) per Regulation (EC) 1005/2008 Article 12?

questions.l1: No benefit-sharing terms are captured or executed; ABS obligations are unmanaged and reporting is absent
questions.l3: Benefit-sharing terms are recorded and some benefits are delivered, but tracking is manual, incomplete across downstream utilization, and reporting is not audit-ready
questions.l5: MAT obligations are recorded per access event, benefit triggers across downstream use are detected and logged, monetary and non-monetary benefits delivered are evidenced, and reports for authorities and partners are generated from the same records
questions.text: Does the agent operationalize ABS benefit-sharing (monetary and non-monetary) under mutually agreed terms (MAT), including tracking obligations, payments/benefits delivery, and reporting, per Nagoya Protocol Article 5?

questions.l1: No fisheries management support; decisions lack science-based objectives, harvest controls, or monitoring evidence
questions.l3: Supports basic fisheries KPIs and references management plans, but harvest controls and ecosystem indicators are incomplete and monitoring evidence is inconsistent
questions.l5: Comprehensive fisheries governance with stock assessment integration, harvest control rules, bycatch/ETP species safeguards, ecosystem indicators, compliance monitoring, and transparent reporting aligned to Art. 7.2
questions.text: Does the agent support fisheries management decision-making consistent with FAO Code of Conduct Art. 7.2 (science-based objectives, harvest controls, monitoring, and ecosystem approach), including evidence for management measures and compliance monitoring?

questions.l1: Forest-product sourcing has no EUDR due diligence
questions.l3: Statements or references are held for some wood products; geolocation is incomplete
questions.l5: Every relevant forest-product lot has a statement/declaration identifier or upstream reference, plot geolocation and a dated deforestation/legality check; lots without them are blocked
questions.text: For wood and other relevant commodities it sources, does the agent hold a due diligence statement (or upstream reference number) with plot geolocation before products are placed on or exported from the EU market, per Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650 (applying from 30 Dec 2026 / 30 Jun 2027)?

questions.l1: Sites are not mapped to national restoration plan measures
questions.l3: Sites are mapped to restoration plan measures, but habitat-condition indicators are not reported against them
questions.l5: Every site is mapped to the plan measures that cover it with the plan version recorded, habitat-condition indicators have baselines and methods, and reports are generated from the same records
questions.text: For sites in an EU Member State, does the agent map each managed site to the measures of the national restoration plan under the Nature Restoration Regulation (EU) 2024/1991 and report habitat-condition indicators for those measures?

questions.l1: Detections of listed species are not flagged or reported
questions.l3: Detections of Union-concern species are flagged, but notification to the competent authority and eradication follow-up are manual and not tracked
questions.l5: Each detection of a Union-concern species is recorded with location, date and evidence, notified to the competent authority with the notification time logged, and the eradication or management outcome is tracked to closure
questions.regulatoryRef: EU IAS Regulation 1143/2014 (early detection and rapid eradication)
questions.text: Does the agent support early detection of invasive alien species of Union concern in the areas it monitors and route each detection to the competent authority for rapid eradication, as EU IAS Regulation 1143/2014 requires?

Loss of traditional art forms through AI-driven curriculum modernization
