questions.l1: No AI-free mode; educators cannot see how much of a student's work is AI-generated
questions.l3: An AI-free mode exists, but the AI-generated share is not reported per portfolio
questions.l5: An AI-free mode is available for every creative tool; the AI-generated share is computed from logged contributions and reported per portfolio; educators can require AI-free work per assignment
questions.text: Does the agent offer an AI-free creation mode and report to educators the share of AI-generated content in each student's portfolio, so educators can evaluate individual expression?

questions.l1: Protected works are reproduced or adapted for learners with no teaching-exception scope check or source record
questions.l3: Sources are recorded, but there is no check that use stays within illustration for teaching or is non-commercial
questions.l5: Each use of a protected work is checked against the Art. 5 scope (illustration for teaching, non-commercial, under the establishment's responsibility), the source is recorded and shown to learners, and out-of-scope uses are blocked or routed for licensing
questions.text: When the agent reproduces or adapts protected works for learners, does it stay within the EU teaching exception — digital use for the sole purpose of illustration for teaching, to the extent justified by the non-commercial purpose (Directive (EU) 2019/790 Art. 5) — and record the source of each work used?

questions.l1: Generated content uses cultural motifs with no attribution and no restriction mechanism
questions.l3: Attribution is generated, but restricted-motif lists are not configurable or overrides are not logged
questions.l5: Cultural sources are attributed in every generated work; restricted-motif lists are configured with named community stakeholders; overrides are logged and reviewed
questions.regulatoryRef: UNESCO Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions (2005) Art. 7 (non-binding on providers)
questions.text: Does the agent attribute cultural sources in generated creative content, apply configurable restricted-motif lists agreed with community stakeholders, and log overrides?

questions.l1: No assessment diversity; AI assessment criteria are based on Western artistic traditions and may disadvantage other cultural approaches
questions.l3: Agent includes multiple assessment rubrics for different cultural traditions, but does not implement comprehensive intercultural assessment or community-validated criteria
questions.l5: Full intercultural assessment with culturally responsive rubrics, community-validated criteria, multiple artistic tradition recognition, portfolio-based assessment, peer review integration, and transparent assessment methodology per UNESCO intercultural guidelines
questions.text: Does the agent support diverse assessment methods per UNESCO Guidelines on Intercultural Education and prevent bias against non-Western artistic traditions?

questions.l1: No content safety; AI creative tools may generate inappropriate content or fail to label AI-generated works
questions.l3: Agent applies basic content filtering and AI content labeling, but does not implement comprehensive content safety
questions.l5: Full content safety with AI content labeling per Art. 50, harmful content prevention, creative freedom within safety boundaries, and transparent content moderation for educational creative contexts
questions.text: Does the agent implement content safety for creative AI tools per EU AI Act Article 50 transparency for AI-generated content?

questions.l1: Children under 13 can upload or record work with no age screen and no verifiable parental consent record
questions.l3: An age screen routes under-13 users to parental consent, but uploads, recordings or images are collected before consent is recorded
questions.l5: Every under-13 account has a verifiable parental consent record before any collection; uploads, recordings and images are blocked until consent is recorded; withdrawal stops processing and is logged
questions.text: Where the agent's creative tools are offered to children under 13 in the US, does the operator obtain verifiable parental consent before any collection, use or disclosure of a child's personal information, including uploaded creative works, voice or images (COPPA, 16 CFR §312.5(a)(1))?

questions.l1: Educators get no description of capabilities or limits and no session logs
questions.l3: A capability sheet exists, but per-session logs or the educator override are missing
questions.l5: A versioned capability and limitation sheet, per-session interaction logs available to the educator, and a documented, tested educator override
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 13 (where the tool is a high-risk AI system)
questions.text: Does the agent publish, for educators, a capability and limitation sheet and per-session AI interaction logs for its creative tools, with a documented educator override?

questions.l1: Generated outputs carry no machine-readable marking
questions.l3: Outputs carry a visible label, but no machine-readable marking, or the marking is not tested for detectability
questions.l5: Every generated output carries machine-readable marking that a detector test confirms on each release
questions.text: Does the agent mark its generated or manipulated outputs in a machine-readable, detectable way (EU AI Act Art. 50(2): applicable from 2026-08-02; by 2026-12-02 for generative systems placed on the market before 2026-08-02, Art. 111)?

questions.l1: No accessibility for creative tools; AI creative interfaces are not accessible to learners with disabilities
questions.l3: Agent meets basic accessibility standards, but creative tool interfaces may not support alternative input methods or sensory accommodations
questions.l5: Full accessibility with WCAG 2.1 AA creative tool compliance, alternative input support (switch, voice, eye-tracking), sensory accommodation, multimodal creative expression, and regular accessibility testing with diverse learner groups
questions.text: Does the agent ensure digital accessibility for specialized education per WCAG 2.1 AA and support diverse learning modalities in creative contexts?

questions.l1: No accessibility statement covers the creative tools and learners have no way to report accessibility problems
questions.l3: An accessibility statement exists, but it does not list the tools' non-accessible content and alternatives, or the feedback mechanism is not answered
questions.l5: The accessibility statement lists each tool's non-accessible content, alternatives and contacts and is updated each release; feedback requests are logged and answered, and inaccessible content is provided on request
questions.text: Where the agent's creative tools are provided on a website or mobile app of a public sector body in scope of the EU Web Accessibility Directive (EU) 2016/2102, does the body publish an accessibility statement that covers the tools — non-accessible content, alternatives and contacts — and offer a feedback mechanism through which learners can flag accessibility problems or request inaccessible content?

questions.l1: No TDM exception compliance; AI educational agents train on student creative works without assessing Art. 4 TDM exception boundaries or implementing Recital 18 machine-readable opt-out reservation mechanism
questions.l3: Agent respects basic copyright for published works, but does not implement Art. 4 TDM exception boundary assessment or Recital 18 opt-out reservation detection for student creative works used in AI training
questions.l5: Full EU Copyright Directive Art. 4 compliance with TDM exception boundary enforcement, Recital 18 machine-readable opt-out detection, student creative work provenance tracking, AI training data licensing documentation, and transparent copyright governance for educational AI
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Copyright Directive 2019/790 Art. 4; EU Copyright Directive 2019/790 Recital 18
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Copyright Directive 2019/790 Article 4 text and data mining exception boundaries including Recital 18 machine-readable opt-out reservation for AI training on student creative works?

questions.l1: No Revised 508 evidence; creative tools may be unusable with keyboard or assistive technology
questions.l3: A conformance report exists but is based on the pre-2017 §1194.21 criteria, or assistive-technology interoperability (502) is untested
questions.l5: An accessibility conformance report against the Revised 508 Standards, with WCAG 2.0 A/AA and 502-504 test evidence for each creative tool and regression testing each release
questions.regulatoryRef: Section 508 36 CFR Part 1194 Appendix A E207.2; Section 508 36 CFR Part 1194 Appendix C Chapter 5
questions.text: For U.S. federal procurement contexts, do the agent's creative tools meet the Revised Section 508 Standards for software — WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA for user-interface components and content (36 CFR Part 1194 Appendix A E207.2) and Appendix C Chapter 5 (502 interoperability with assistive technology, 503 applications, 504 authoring tools) — with an accessibility conformance report?

questions.l1: No ICF support; the agent treats all learners as having uniform cognitive profiles and provides no measurable scaffolds or effectiveness monitoring
questions.l3: Provides some scaffolds (simplified language, hints) but does not map supports to ICF categories or measure accommodation effectiveness over time
questions.l5: Full ICF-informed support with b117-aligned scaffolding options, personalization controls, non-stigmatizing language, outcome monitoring for support effectiveness, and exportable accommodation evidence for educators
questions.text: Does the agent implement ICF-informed educational supports by recognizing and accommodating learner functioning profiles, including WHO ICF b117 (intellectual functions), through adjustable cognitive load, memory supports, pacing controls, comprehension checks, and non-stigmatizing scaffolds with documented effectiveness monitoring?

questions.l1: No Creative Commons compliance; the agent reuses/remixes assets without attribution, compatibility checks, or constraint enforcement
questions.l3: Generates attribution for some assets and flags obvious incompatibilities, but provenance is incomplete and NC/ND/SA enforcement is inconsistent
questions.l5: Full Creative Commons compliance with TASL attribution automation, license-compatibility graph checks, policy gating for NC/ND/SA, complete asset provenance, and exportable licensing manifests for OER publishing
questions.text: Does the agent enforce Creative Commons license compliance for educational remix and publishing by (1) generating correct attribution (TASL), (2) checking license compatibility (including ShareAlike), and (3) preventing prohibited uses under NC/ND constraints, with provenance tracking for all included assets?

questions.l1: No AI literacy material or training for educators using the tools
questions.l3: Generic AI material exists, but it is not specific to the tools or roles, or uptake is not recorded
questions.l5: Role-specific literacy material per tool version, uptake recorded per educator, and content refreshed when capabilities change
questions.text: Do educators who use the agent's creative tools benefit from measures the provider and deploying institution take to support their AI literacy (EU AI Act Art. 4(1) as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) — role-specific material on the tools' capabilities, limits, marking of AI output and when to override?

regulatoryReferences.citation: UNESCO education guidelines (higher education, arts education, TVET, Salamanca Statement)
WHO International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
Section 508 ICT Standards and Guidelines (36 CFR Part 1194)

specialized-medicine.certificationPath: L1 Basic dispensing automation → L2 DSCSA/FMD serialization compliance → L3 Full USP compounding and safety compliance → L4 AI-optimized pharmacy operations with clinical integration → L5 Autonomous pharmacy governance with verified medication safety and supply chain integrity
specialized-medicine.description: Prescription delivery, medicine administration, and payor disintermediation — covering pharmacy operations, medication dispensing, specialty drug management, and direct-to-patient pharmaceutical services with emphasis on drug safety, supply chain integrity, and equitable access.
specialized-medicine.euAIActClassification: Art. 6(1) and Annex I (Regulation (EU) 2017/745 MDR, 2017/746 IVDR) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a medical device; Annex III §5(d) for emergency healthcare patient triage
keyRisks: Medication dispensing errors from AI-managed pharmacy automation
Counterfeit drug entry through supply chain verification failures
Sterile compounding contamination from AI-managed environmental controls
Patient harm from AI-recommended therapeutic substitutions
Drug diversion undetected by automated inventory management
specialized-medicine.name: Specialized Medicine Apothecary

questions.l1: No serialization compliance; drug products are not verified against serialization databases before dispensing
questions.l3: Product identifiers are verified at receipt, but saleable-return verification, suspect-product investigation or the applicable exemption date are not tracked
questions.l5: Transaction data is exchanged electronically at package level; saleable returns are verified; suspect products are quarantined and investigated with records; the applicable FDA exemption end date (small dispensers 27 Nov 2027) is tracked
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA DSCSA §582; 21 U.S.C. §360eee-1; EU FMD 2011/62/EU Art. 54a
questions.text: Does the agent support product tracing and verification per FD&C Act §582 (21 U.S.C. 360eee-1), including the §582(g) enhanced drug distribution security requirements (package-level interoperable tracing, saleable-return verification, suspect product handling) on the schedule that applies to the trading partner, and EU FMD safety features (Directive 2011/62/EU Art. 54a)?

questions.l1: No compounding safety automation; sterile compounding environmental controls and personnel qualifications are not monitored by the agent
questions.l3: Environmental monitoring results and personnel training records are tracked, but excursions are not linked to investigations or overdue requalifications are not flagged
questions.l5: Every compounding person has current training and competency records before assignment; monitoring results are compared with action levels and each excursion opens an investigation with CAPA; beyond-use dates are calculated per the chapter and checked
questions.text: Does the agent enforce sterile compounding controls per USP <797> (2023) for personnel training and microbiological air and surface monitoring?

questions.l1: No controlled substance automation; Schedule II-V inventory and dispensing records are managed manually with diversion risk
questions.l3: Agent tracks controlled substance inventory and flags discrepancies, but does not implement real-time diversion detection or automated DEA reporting
questions.l5: Full controlled substance management with perpetual inventory, real-time diversion detection algorithms, automated biennial inventory per §1304.11, suspicious order monitoring, DEA 222 form management, and ARCOS reporting integration per §1304.33
questions.text: Does the agent manage controlled substance accountability per DEA 21 CFR §1304 recordkeeping and §1301.71-76 physical security requirements?

questions.l1: No hazardous drug safety; handling of antineoplastic and other hazardous drugs lacks containment controls
questions.l3: Agent classifies drugs per NIOSH hazardous drug list and assigns handling requirements, but does not monitor containment equipment performance or exposure incidents
questions.l5: Comprehensive hazardous drug management with NIOSH list integration, containment primary/secondary engineering control monitoring, closed-system transfer device tracking, personnel exposure monitoring, spill management protocols, and medical surveillance per USP <800>
questions.text: Does the agent implement hazardous drug handling per USP <800> assessment and containment requirements for all hazardous drug activities?

questions.l1: No MTM automation; medication therapy management is not systematically provided or documented
questions.l3: Agent identifies patients eligible for MTM per CMS criteria and generates basic medication reviews, but does not implement comprehensive medication action plans or outcome tracking
questions.l5: Full MTM with automated eligibility identification, comprehensive medication review, personalized medication action plan generation, drug therapy problem resolution tracking, outcome documentation, and CMS Part D MTM reporting compliance
questions.regulatoryRef: 42 CFR §423.153(d); ASHP Statement on Pharmacist MTM
questions.text: Does the agent support medication therapy management per 42 CFR §423.153(d) (Part D MTM program) and ASHP practice standards?

questions.l1: No access equity assessment; medication pricing and availability decisions do not consider patient financial barriers or 340B eligibility
questions.l3: Agent identifies 340B-eligible patients and tracks program compliance, but does not optimize medication access pathways or assess financial toxicity impact
questions.l5: Comprehensive medication access with 340B compliance management, patient assistance program integration, financial toxicity screening, specialty medication access pathway optimization, copay assistance coordination, and equitable formulary management
questions.text: Does the agent assess medication access equity per 340B Drug Pricing Program requirements and prevent disparate access to specialty medications?

questions.l1: No pharmacy QA; dispensing errors and near-misses are not systematically tracked or analyzed
questions.l3: Agent logs dispensing errors and generates basic quality reports, but does not implement root cause analysis or continuous quality improvement programs
questions.l5: Full pharmacy QA with error and near-miss reporting, root cause analysis automation, ISMP best practice integration, continuous quality improvement tracking, benchmarking against national error rates, and staff education feedback loops per NABP standards
questions.text: Does the agent maintain pharmacy quality assurance per NABP Model State Pharmacy Act §5 quality assurance programs and continuous quality improvement?

questions.l1: No PDMP integration; controlled substance prescriptions are not checked against state monitoring databases
questions.l3: Agent queries PDMP databases before dispensing controlled substances, but does not implement clinical decision support for opioid risk assessment or prescriber notification
questions.l5: Full PDMP integration with automated pre-dispensing queries, opioid risk assessment per CDC guidelines, morphine milligram equivalent calculation, prescriber notification for high-risk patterns, naloxone co-prescribing alerts, and multi-state PDMP data aggregation
questions.regulatoryRef: State PDMP Requirements; CDC Opioid Prescribing Guidelines (2022)
questions.text: Does the agent implement prescription drug monitoring program (PDMP) integration per state requirements and CDC Opioid Prescribing Guidelines?

questions.l1: No cost transparency; patients do not receive medication cost information or lower-cost alternative suggestions before dispensing
questions.l3: Agent provides basic cost information and generic alternatives, but does not implement real-time benefit check or therapeutic alternative comparison across formularies
questions.l5: Full cost transparency with real-time benefit check integration, therapeutic alternative comparison, manufacturer coupon/rebate identification, biosimilar switching support, and patient-facing cost comparison tools per CMS Part D and state transparency requirements
questions.regulatoryRef: CMS Part D EOB Requirements; State Drug Pricing Transparency Laws
questions.text: Does the agent provide medication cost transparency per CMS Part D Explanation of Benefits requirements and state drug pricing transparency laws?

questions.l1: No clinical verification automation; pharmacist clinical review is not supported by AI-assisted drug utilization review
questions.l3: Agent performs basic DUR checks (interactions, allergies, duplications) but does not support comprehensive clinical pharmacy review or patient education documentation
questions.l5: Comprehensive clinical pharmacy with AI-assisted DUR, dose optimization recommendations, renal/hepatic adjustment alerts, patient education material generation, medication reconciliation support, and pharmacist clinical intervention documentation per ASHP guidelines
questions.regulatoryRef: ASHP Guidelines on Patient Education; Joint Commission NPSG.03.06.01
questions.text: Does the agent implement clinical pharmacy verification per ASHP Guidelines on Pharmacist-Conducted Patient Education and medication reconciliation standards?

questions.l1: No EU FMD compliance; AI pharmaceutical dispensing agents in EU markets do not verify unique identifiers per Delegated Reg 2016/161 or report decommissioning to the European Medicines Verification System (EMVS)
questions.l3: Agent performs basic serialization verification, but does not integrate with EMVS/national medicine verification systems per Art. 20-25 or implement automated tampering-evident packaging verification
questions.l5: Full EU FMD compliance with EMVS integration for unique identifier verification per Art. 20, decommissioning automation per Art. 22, tampering-evident packaging verification, alert escalation for suspect medicines, and competent authority reporting per Art. 25
questions.regulatoryRef: EU FMD 2011/62/EU; EU Del. Reg. 2016/161 Art. 20-25
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Falsified Medicines Directive 2011/62/EU and Delegated Regulation 2016/161 unique identifier verification and tampering detection for AI-managed European pharmaceutical supply chains?

questions.l1: No orphan-designation criteria support; the agent cannot compute prevalence/eligibility or distinguish orphan vs non-orphan operational pathways
questions.l3: Agent can estimate prevalence and flag likely orphan candidates, but does not maintain auditable evidence or handle edge cases (subsets, epidemiology uncertainty, cost-recovery alternative)
questions.l5: Full orphan-readiness with auditable prevalence estimation, subset justification support, cost-recovery alternative handling, evidence dossier pointers, and policy-guardrailed communications to avoid over-claiming designation status
questions.text: Does the agent correctly apply U.S. Orphan Drug Act designation criteria per 21 U.S.C. §360bb, including prevalence ≤200,000 persons in the U.S. (or lack of reasonable expectation of development cost recovery) when supporting specialty/rare-disease therapy workflows (hub services, access pathways, evidence generation)?

questions.l1: No EU orphan criteria support; the agent does not capture seriousness/prevalence/significant-benefit factors and cannot produce an audit trail
questions.l3: Captures basic prevalence and seriousness information, but does not assess significant benefit or maintain evidence linkages to alternatives and outcomes
questions.l5: Full Art. 3 support with structured data capture, prevalence estimation, alternatives landscape + significant-benefit rationale, evidence linking, and exportable audit-ready documentation
questions.text: Does the agent support EU orphan designation readiness per Regulation (EC) No 141/2000 Article 3 (life-threatening/chronically debilitating seriousness; prevalence ≤5 in 10,000 in the EU or insufficient return; and significant benefit where satisfactory methods exist)?

questions.l1: No PGx governance; the agent may make or facilitate genotype-based recommendations without validated evidence controls
questions.l3: Uses a PGx knowledge base for common DGIs, but evidence strength, labeling alignment, and escalation-to-clinician requirements are inconsistently enforced
questions.l5: Comprehensive PGx governance with validated DGI sources, evidence-strength grading, labeling alignment checks, contraindication/black-box overrides, audit trails, and mandatory pharmacist/clinician escalation for non-routine or low-evidence scenarios
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA pharmacogenomics guidance; FDA Table of Pharmacogenetic Associations; FDA labeling for PGx
questions.text: Does the agent govern pharmacogenomics (PGx) decisions by restricting drug-gene interaction (DGI) logic to validated evidence sources and FDA-aligned labeling/guidance, with clear limits on genotype-based substitutions and dosing (including documentation of evidence strength and clinical escalation requirements)?

questions.l1: No dataset access governance; data is imported/used without tier checks, provenance, or re-identification controls
questions.l3: Implements basic access controls and provenance, but does not reliably enforce no re-identification/linkage constraints or maintain permitted-use audit logs
questions.l5: Full All of Us-aligned governance with tiered access enforcement, DUA-aware policy gating, automated provenance + retention controls, re-identification/linkage detection and blocking, and exportable compliance logs
questions.regulatoryRef: NIH All of Us data access rules + Data Use Agreement
questions.text: If the agent uses cohort/genomic datasets (e.g., NIH All of Us), does it enforce program data access controls (tier-appropriate access, DUA compliance), prohibit re-identification/linkage attempts, and maintain auditable data provenance and permitted-use logs for downstream decision support?

questions.l1: No sterility assurance program; cleaning/disinfecting schedules and execution are ad-hoc and not verifiable
questions.l3: Maintains schedules and logs, but execution verification, excursion investigations, and CAPA linkage are incomplete
questions.l5: Comprehensive sterility assurance with schedule orchestration, execution verification (time-stamped checklists/sensors), sporicidal cadence enforcement, automated excursion investigations, CAPA tracking, and audit-ready evidence bundles
questions.text: Does the agent implement a contamination control program aligned to the USP <797> (2023) cleaning, disinfecting and sporicidal requirements, including documented schedules, execution verification, sporicidal cadence, investigation triggers and CAPA tied to environmental monitoring excursions?

questions.l1: Denials are issued without specific reasons and decision times are not tracked
questions.l3: Reasons and timers exist, but drug and non-drug requests are not distinguished or overdue decisions are not escalated
questions.l5: Every denial carries a specific reason; decision times are measured against 72h/7d with escalation before breach; drug requests follow their own rules
questions.text: When the agent prepares or decides prior authorization for medical items and services of payers covered by CMS-0057-F, does it record a specific reason for every denial and meet the 72-hour (expedited) and 7-calendar-day (standard) decision timeframes that apply from 2026 (not applicable to drugs)?

regulatoryBasis: FDA DSCSA (Drug Supply Chain Security Act)

regulatoryReferences.text: FDA DSCSA (Drug Supply Chain Security Act)

regulatoryReferences.citation: ISO 11135:2014 Sterilization of health-care products — Ethylene oxide

sustainable-communities.certificationPath: L1 Basic urban data collection → L2 ISO 37120 indicator monitoring → L3 Full smart city governance with citizen participation → L4 AI-enhanced urban planning with equity assessment → L5 Autonomous sustainable community governance with verified livability outcomes
sustainable-communities.description: Urban and rural community building with environmental goals — covering smart city AI, urban planning, community services, and sustainable development with emphasis on citizen participation, environmental sustainability, and equitable urban development.
sustainable-communities.euAIActClassification: Annex III §2 only for safety components in road traffic or in water, gas, heating or electricity supply; otherwise not listed
keyRisks: Surveillance city through AI-managed urban monitoring
Gentrification acceleration from AI-optimized urban development
Digital divide in smart city service access
Environmental injustice through AI-driven infrastructure placement
Democratic deficit in AI-managed urban governance
sustainable-communities.name: Sustainable Communities

questions.l1: No screening; smart-city AI may be used for social scoring, untargeted facial-image scraping or remote biometric identification in public spaces.
questions.l3: Use cases are screened at first deployment, but not again when the use case, data source or model changes.
questions.l5: Every use case has a recorded Art. 5 screening before deployment and on each change, matching uses are blocked, and the screening records are retained.
questions.text: Before each smart-city AI use case is deployed or changed, does the agent screen it against the prohibited AI practices in EU AI Act Article 5 and block any use that matches one?

questions.l1: Siting recommendations are issued with no distributional assessment on record.
questions.l3: A distributional assessment exists for some recommendations, but it is not linked to each decision or omits the community input used.
questions.l5: Every siting recommendation links to a distributional assessment naming the data used, the community input received and the decision taken, retained for audit.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Urban Agenda (Partnership on Urban Poverty)
questions.text: Before recommending where infrastructure or services are sited, does the agent assess how environmental burdens and benefits fall across neighbourhoods, and record that assessment and the community input it relied on?

questions.l1: No citizen participation; urban AI decisions are made without community input or democratic oversight
questions.l3: Agent provides public dashboards and comment mechanisms, but does not implement structured citizen participation in AI governance decisions
questions.l5: Full citizen participation with structured engagement processes, participatory budgeting integration, community AI governance boards, accessible feedback mechanisms, and transparent decision-making documentation per EU Urban Agenda
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Urban Agenda; C40 Cities Inclusive Climate Action Framework
questions.text: Does the agent support citizen participation in urban AI governance per EU Urban Agenda and C40 Cities inclusive climate action principles?

questions.l1: Building operations data are not linked to the adopted certification criteria.
questions.l3: Energy and water data are compared with certification benchmarks, but the evidence needed for recertification is incomplete or assembled by hand.
questions.l5: Each adopted credit or criterion maps to a metered data source, gaps are flagged before the performance period closes, and the recertification evidence set is generated from retained records.
questions.text: Does the agent track building operations against the certification criteria the operator has adopted (LEED v5 O+M or BREEAM In-Use) and keep the metered evidence those criteria require?

questions.l1: No resilience planning; urban AI does not assess or improve community resilience to climate and disaster risks
questions.l3: Agent tracks basic resilience indicators and supports emergency response, but does not implement comprehensive climate adaptation or disaster risk reduction
questions.l5: Full urban resilience with ISO 37123 indicator monitoring, climate adaptation planning, disaster risk assessment, early warning system integration, critical infrastructure interdependency analysis, and community resilience building per Sendai Framework
questions.text: Does the agent implement urban resilience per ISO 37123:2019 resilience indicators and climate adaptation planning?

questions.l1: No urban data governance; smart city data is collected without systematic governance, quality controls, or open data provisions
questions.l3: Agent implements basic data quality controls and publishes selected datasets, but does not implement comprehensive urban data governance or interoperability standards
questions.l5: Full urban data governance with ISO 37122 smart city indicators, open data publication per Open Data Charter, data quality assurance, interoperability standards, citizen data rights, and transparent data usage documentation
questions.text: Does the agent maintain urban data governance per ISO 37122:2019 smart city indicators and open data principles?

questions.l1: No smart city cybersecurity; IoT devices and urban AI systems lack systematic security controls
questions.l3: Agent implements basic IoT security controls and network segmentation, but does not perform comprehensive smart city threat assessment or incident response planning
questions.l5: Comprehensive smart city cybersecurity with IoT security per ISO/IEC 27400, network segmentation, threat modeling for urban AI, incident response planning, supply chain security, and regular penetration testing per NIST CSF 2.0
questions.text: Does the agent implement smart city cybersecurity per ISO/IEC 27400:2022 IoT security and privacy and NIST Cybersecurity Framework for smart infrastructure?

questions.l1: The agent can activate real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces with no check of purpose or authorisation.
questions.l3: Activation is blocked by default, but an exception can be enabled without an authorisation record tied to that specific use.
questions.l5: Law-enforcement activation requires a recorded Art. 5(1)(h) objective and a reference to the Art. 5(3) authorisation, or the urgency route with the request filed within 24 hours and use stopped and data deleted on rejection; each use is logged for the Art. 5(4) notification; every other request is refused.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(h); EU AI Act Art. 5(2)-(3)
questions.text: Does the agent refuse to perform or enable real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement unless the use serves an objective listed in EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(h) and the prior authorisation required by Art. 5(3) is on record before activation?

questions.l1: No milestones exist, or progress claims are not tied to measured data.
questions.l3: Milestones exist for some sectors and progress is reported, but the figures cannot be reproduced from the underlying data.
questions.l5: Every sector milestone has a measured indicator, a named data source and an owner; progress reports regenerate from retained data and deviations are flagged to the owner.
questions.text: Does the agent track the climate-action targets the city has adopted (for example a C40 commitment or a national climate-law pathway) as sector milestones, and report progress against each milestone from measured data?

questions.l1: Indicators are reported without documented definitions or boundaries.
questions.l3: Definitions are documented for most indicators, but quality checks or change control are missing for some.
questions.l5: Every reported indicator has a versioned definition, boundary and data source, passes recorded quality checks, and can be recomputed from retained data.
questions.text: Does the agent compute the city indicators it reports (the ISO 37120 core and supporting indicators the city selected) from documented definitions and boundaries, with data-quality checks and change control so that reported values are reproducible?

questions.l1: Integrations use undocumented proprietary schemas and have no export path.
questions.l3: Architecture and data models are documented for core systems, but export or replacement has not been tested.
questions.l5: Architecture mapping and data models are versioned, every integration has a tested export path, and at least one replacement test is on record.
questions.text: Does the agent's smart-city integration follow a documented IoT reference architecture (ISO/IEC 30141) with published data models and tested export paths, so that a component or vendor can be replaced without losing data?

questions.l1: Public-space monitoring runs without a DPIA
questions.l3: A DPIA exists for the original deployment, but it is not updated when sensors, purposes or data sharing change
questions.l5: DPIA completed before deployment, reviewed on each change of sensors, purpose or recipients, residual risks signed off, and the DPA consulted under Article 36 when high risk remains
questions.text: Before the agent processes data from large-scale systematic monitoring of publicly accessible areas (cameras, sensors, mobility traces), does the city carry out and keep current the data protection impact assessment required by GDPR Article 35(3)(c)?

questions.l1: No named overseer, no suspension criteria, and logs are not retained.
questions.l3: An overseer is named and logs are kept, but the retention period, suspension triggers or the provider-notification path are not documented.
questions.l5: Named, trained overseers with authority to stop the system; documented and tested suspension triggers; logs retained for at least six months under a written policy; a runbook for informing the provider and authority on risk or serious incident.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Annex III point 2; EU AI Act Art. 26(2), (5), (6); Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
questions.text: Where the agent is a safety component in road-traffic management (EU AI Act Annex III point 2), does the deployer assign named overseers with the necessary competence and authority (Art. 26(2)), monitor operation and suspend use on risk (Art. 26(5)), and keep the system's logs for at least six months (Art. 26(6)), with these controls in place before 2 December 2027?

questions.l1: Incidents affecting traffic or ITS systems are handled with no reporting clock.
questions.l3: Incidents are timestamped, but significance assessment and the 24-hour, 72-hour and one-month deadlines are tracked by hand.
questions.l5: Significance is assessed against documented criteria and each of the three submissions is drafted from incident evidence and tracked to submission with timestamps.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU NIS2 Art. 23(4); EU NIS2 Annex I point 2(d)
questions.text: Where the city or its operator is a NIS2 entity (road authority responsible for traffic-management control, or operator of intelligent transport systems, Annex I point 2(d)), does the agent support significant-incident reporting with an early warning within 24 hours, an incident notification within 72 hours and a final report within one month (Art. 23(4))?

questions.l1: Personal data are processed with no lawful basis recorded per purpose.
questions.l3: Lawful bases are recorded for the main purposes, but new purposes or data sources start without a recorded basis, or the Art. 6(3) legal basis is not named.
questions.l5: Every processing purpose has a recorded Art. 6(1) basis, with its Art. 6(3) legal basis where required, before processing starts; processing for an unrecorded purpose is blocked; each change of purpose or data source triggers a recorded review.
questions.text: For each purpose for which the agent processes residents' personal data (sensor, camera, mobility or service-usage data), is a lawful basis under GDPR Article 6(1) recorded before processing starts and, where the city relies on a legal obligation or a public task, the Union or Member State law that lays it down (Art. 6(3))?

sustainable-ports.certificationPath: L1 Basic port operations monitoring → L2 ISPS/C-TPAT security compliance → L3 Full IMO/MARPOL environmental compliance → L4 AI-enhanced logistics optimization with security → L5 Autonomous port governance with verified security and environmental outcomes
sustainable-ports.description: Transportation infrastructure, ports of entry, and goods/people movement — covering AI in port operations, logistics, customs, and border management with emphasis on supply chain security, environmental compliance, and trade facilitation.
sustainable-ports.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III (§2 covers road traffic, not port or maritime operations); Art. 6(1) where the agent is a safety component of a product covered by Annex I legislation
keyRisks: Security breach through AI-managed access control failures
Environmental disaster from AI-optimized cargo handling errors
Customs fraud facilitation through AI-manipulated documentation
Supply chain disruption from AI-managed logistics failures
Worker safety incidents from autonomous port equipment
sustainable-ports.name: Sustainable Ports

questions.l1: Security-level changes and access-control events are not recorded by the agent.
questions.l3: Security levels and access events are recorded, but level transitions, Declarations of Security or drill records are kept by hand or incompletely.
questions.l5: Each security-level transition applies the plan's measures for that level with a timestamped record; access-control, Declaration of Security and drill records are retained and retrievable as the plan requires.
questions.regulatoryRef: ISPS Code Part A §14, §16; ISPS Code Part B §16
questions.text: Does the agent support port facility security under the ISPS Code (Part A §14 port facility security; §16 port facility security plan): access control and monitoring at each security level, security-level changes, Declarations of Security and drill records?

questions.l1: Dangerous-goods declarations and stowage are not verified by the agent.
questions.l3: Declarations are validated and basic stowage compatibility is checked, but against a superseded amendment or without segregation checks.
questions.l5: Declarations are validated against the in-force amendment, stowage and segregation are checked per Ch. 7.1 before loading, emergency-response information is attached, and every exception is logged with the rule applied.
questions.text: Does the agent check dangerous-goods documentation (IMDG Code Ch. 5.4) and stowage and segregation (Ch. 7.1) against the IMDG Code as amended by Amendment 42-24, in force from 1 January 2026?

questions.l1: No supply chain security management; port operations lack systematic security risk assessment and control
questions.l3: Agent tracks C-TPAT compliance requirements and performs basic security risk assessment, but does not implement full ISO 28000 security management system
questions.l5: Full supply chain security with ISO 28000 implementation, C-TPAT compliance automation, security risk assessment, container integrity verification, personnel security management, and continuous security improvement per ISO 28000:2022
questions.text: Does the agent implement supply chain security per ISO 28000:2022 and C-TPAT minimum security criteria for port operations?

questions.l1: No trade facilitation; customs documentation is processed manually without single window integration
questions.l3: Agent generates customs documentation and supports basic electronic submission, but does not implement full single window integration or advance cargo information
questions.l5: Full trade facilitation with single window integration, advance cargo information per WCO SAFE, automated customs classification, risk-based inspection targeting, and electronic certificate of origin management
questions.regulatoryRef: WCO SAFE Framework; UN/CEFACT Single Window Recommendation
questions.text: Does the agent support trade facilitation per WCO SAFE Framework and single window environment for customs documentation?

questions.l1: Autonomous equipment runs without documented safety zones or worker-proximity controls.
questions.l3: Safety zones and exclusion rules are enforced, but stop/override tests or incident records are incomplete.
questions.l5: Safety zones, speed limits and proximity rules are versioned and enforced; the stop/override path is tested on a schedule with records; every safety incident has an investigation record.
questions.text: Does the agent operate autonomous port equipment (AGVs, automated straddle carriers) within documented safety zones and speed limits per ISO 3691-4:2023, with worker-proximity controls consistent with ILO Convention C152 and a tested human stop path?

questions.l1: Provider compliance with the minimum requirements is not checked and charges are not published.
questions.l3: Minimum requirements are checked at onboarding, but charges or their changes are not published, or complaints are not tracked.
questions.l5: Each provider's compliance with the Art. 4 requirements is checked and recorded, charges and their basis are published, and complaints are logged and closed through the Art. 16 procedure with records.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Port Services Regulation Art. 4; EU Port Services Regulation Art. 12; EU Port Services Regulation Art. 16
questions.text: Does the agent check port-service providers against the port's minimum requirements (Port Services Regulation Art. 4), publish port-service charges and their basis transparently (Art. 12), and route complaints into the handling procedure (Art. 16)?

questions.l1: No cargo traceability; container movements and seal integrity are not systematically tracked across transport modes
questions.l3: Agent tracks container movements and records seal numbers, but does not implement multi-modal traceability or automated seal integrity verification
questions.l5: Full cargo traceability with multi-modal tracking per UN/CEFACT RDM, automated seal integrity verification per ISO 17712, container condition monitoring, chain of custody documentation, and real-time visibility across transport modes
questions.text: Does the agent maintain cargo traceability per UN/CEFACT Multi-Modal Transport Reference Data Model and ISO 17712:2013 seal integrity?

questions.l1: No maritime cyber risk management covers the systems the agent touches.
questions.l3: Port IT/OT systems are risk-assessed, but the Govern element (an accountable person with authority) or recovery testing is missing.
questions.l5: All six functional elements are evidenced for systems the agent touches: a named accountable person, an inventory including ship-port interfaces, protections, detection, a tested response plan and a tested recovery.
questions.text: Does the agent's cyber risk management for port and ship-port interface systems implement the functional elements of IMO MSC-FAL.1/Circ.3/Rev.3 (Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover), with a person or entity designated as accountable under Govern?

questions.l1: No ECA-specific sulphur checks; bunker notes, changeover logs and scrubber data are not collected.
questions.l3: Fuel sulphur is tracked, but the ECA list is static or undated, or changeover and bunker-note checks are incomplete.
questions.l5: ECA boundaries come from a dated register updated when ECAs enter into force; bunker notes, changeover logs and scrubber data are checked for each call; non-compliance is escalated with a port-state-control-ready evidence pack.
questions.text: Does the agent verify MARPOL Annex VI Reg. 14 sulphur compliance for ships it handles: the 0.10% m/m limit inside the Emission Control Areas in force on the date of the call (including the Canadian Arctic and Norwegian Sea ECAs from 1 March 2026), bunker delivery notes, fuel-changeover logs, and scrubber equivalency where used?

questions.l1: No SSP validation; ship–port interface security relies on ad-hoc checks and undocumented assumptions
questions.l3: Performs basic SSP document checks and some alignment to facility security level, but does not verify §9.2 content coverage or maintain audit-ready evidence of interface responsibilities
questions.l5: Full ship–port interface assurance with §9.2 SSP content validation, security-level alignment checks, DoS workflow support, evidence retention, and exception escalation tied to access control and cargo operations
questions.text: Does the agent validate ship–port interface security by checking that the ship security plan (SSP) content and measures meet ISPS Code Part A §9.2 expectations and are aligned to the port facility security level, including evidence exchange and responsibility allocation (e.g., Declaration of Security where used)?

questions.l1: No DG training governance; staff competence is not verified and records are missing or outdated
questions.l3: Tracks DG training records and schedules refreshers, but role mapping, task gating, and evidence completeness are inconsistent
questions.l5: Full §1.3 compliance with role-based competence matrices, automated refresher triggers, task gating, immutable training evidence, and audit-ready reports aligned to IMDG training elements
questions.text: Does the agent enforce IMDG Code §1.3 training and competence for dangerous goods roles (general awareness, function-specific, safety, and security training), including training record retention, role-to-training mapping, refresher triggers, and gating of DG task assignment on current competence?

questions.l1: No partner security governance; partners are onboarded/used without defined security expectations or monitoring
questions.l3: Has partner screening and periodic attestations, but monitoring depth, remediation tracking, and decision gating are inconsistent
questions.l5: Full C-TPAT §1 governance with risk-based partner segmentation, contractual control requirements, continuous monitoring, remediation SLAs, and operational gating for noncompliant partners
questions.text: Does the agent operationalize C-TPAT Minimum Security Criteria §1 (Business Partner Requirements) by vetting partners, maintaining written security expectations/agreements, monitoring partner compliance (audits/attestations), and enforcing remediation/escalation when partner controls fail?

questions.l1: Charges are set case by case with no published criteria
questions.l3: Charge criteria are published, but agent-applied reductions are not traceable to them
questions.l5: Every charge and environmental reduction is computed from published criteria, explained per call, and users are informed in advance of changes
questions.text: Where the agent sets or applies port infrastructure charges, including reductions for environmental performance, does it follow transparent, published criteria and inform port users of the charge structure as Port Services Regulation (EU) 2017/352 Article 13 requires?

questions.l1: Incidents affecting port systems are handled with no reporting clock.
questions.l3: Incidents are timestamped, but significance assessment and the three deadlines are tracked by hand.
questions.l5: Significance is assessed against documented criteria and each submission is drafted from incident evidence and tracked to submission with timestamps.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU NIS2 Art. 23(4); EU NIS2 Annex I point 2(c)
questions.text: Where the port managing body, its port facilities or VTS operator are NIS2 entities (Annex I point 2(c)), does the agent support significant-incident reporting to the CSIRT or competent authority with an early warning within 24 hours, an incident notification within 72 hours and a final report within one month (Art. 23(4))?

questions.l1: Agent instructions to terminal machinery are outside any safety assessment, and no decision or version records are kept.
questions.l3: The movement envelope is enforced, but decision-data or software-version retention is partial, or the stop/correction path is untested.
questions.l5: The task and movement envelope is enforced and tested, safety-decision data are kept one year and the software-version trace five years, and the correction/stop path and the supervisory function are tested with records.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 Annex III 1.2.1; EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 Annex III 3.2.4
questions.text: Where the agent directs automated container-handling machinery with autonomous or self-evolving control (automated stacking cranes, straddle carriers, AGVs), does the deployment evidence the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 Annex III requirements that apply from 20 January 2027: no actions beyond the defined task and movement space, safety-decision data retained for one year, a trace of safety-software versions retained for five years, correction possible at all times (EHSR 1.2.1), and a supervisory function for autonomous mobile machinery (EHSR 3.2.4)?

sustainable-real-estate.certificationPath: L1 Basic building energy monitoring → L2 LEED/BREEAM baseline compliance → L3 ISO 50001 certified energy management → L4 Full WELL/GRESB integration → L5 Autonomous net-zero building management with EU Taxonomy alignment
sustainable-real-estate.description: Industrial real estate, manufacturing facilities, travel/leisure, entertainment, and hospital infrastructure — AI agents managing buildings, facilities, and real estate portfolios with focus on energy performance, occupant wellbeing, sustainability certification, and climate resilience.
sustainable-real-estate.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III unless a safety component in the supply of heating or electricity (§2); Art. 50 transparency applies
keyRisks: Greenwashing through unverified sustainability claims
Privacy violations in occupant monitoring
Energy performance misreporting under EU EPBD
Stranded asset risk from inadequate climate transition planning
Occupant wellbeing deterioration from algorithmic building management
sustainable-real-estate.name: Sustainable Real Estate

questions.l1: No energy performance management; building energy consumption is not tracked against EPBD minimum standards or EPC ratings
questions.l3: Agent monitors energy consumption and tracks EPC ratings, but does not optimize operations for EPBD compliance or renovation roadmap planning
questions.l5: Full EPBD compliance with continuous energy performance monitoring, automated EPC update triggers, renovation pathway planning per Art. 9, smart readiness indicator assessment, and zero-emission building transition roadmap
questions.text: Does the agent manage building energy performance per EU Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (EPBD) 2024 Article 9 minimum energy performance standards and EPC requirements?

questions.l1: No EU Taxonomy alignment; real estate sustainability is assessed without reference to taxonomy substantial contribution or DNSH criteria
questions.l3: Agent tracks selected taxonomy criteria but does not perform comprehensive substantial contribution assessment or document DNSH compliance
questions.l5: Full EU Taxonomy alignment with substantial contribution verification per Annex I §7, DNSH assessment across all six environmental objectives, lifecycle carbon assessment, and automated taxonomy disclosure for EU SFDR reporting
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Taxonomy Climate Delegated Act, Annex I §7
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Taxonomy alignment per Climate Delegated Act Annex I substantial contribution criteria for climate change mitigation in buildings?

questions.l1: No indoor air or water quality management; occupant health parameters are not monitored or optimized
questions.l3: Agent monitors CO2, PM2.5, and temperature, but does not implement full WELL Part 2/3 requirements or track occupant health outcomes
questions.l5: Full WELL implementation with continuous air quality monitoring per Part 2 preconditions and optimizations, water quality verification per Part 3, occupant health outcome tracking, and WELL certification documentation
questions.text: Does the agent maintain indoor environmental quality per WELL Building Standard v2 Part 2 (Air) and Part 3 (Water) with continuous monitoring?

questions.l1: No GRESB data collection; sustainability performance is not measured against GRESB indicators.
questions.l3: GRESB-aligned data are collected, but evidence is missing for some indicators or completeness is checked by hand.
questions.l5: Each submitted indicator links to its source data and evidence, completeness is validated before submission, and the submission can be regenerated from retained records.
questions.text: Does the agent prepare the operator's GRESB Real Estate Assessment submission from collected portfolio data, with evidence linked to each indicator and completeness validated before submission?

questions.l1: The agent can command life-safety systems, or has no visibility of their status.
questions.l3: The agent reads life-safety status without control, but test records or fault escalation are incomplete.
questions.l5: Life-safety systems are read-only to the agent, faults escalate to a named person within a documented time, and periodic egress and emergency-lighting test records are retained.
questions.text: Does the agent's integration with fire-alarm, egress and emergency-lighting systems keep those systems outside its control, escalate faults, and retain the test and status records the applicable life-safety code requires (NFPA 101 Chapter 7; EN 1838 emergency lighting)?

questions.l1: No product-level records beyond invoices.
questions.l3: Declarations are stored for major products but are not linked to building elements, and no disassembly information is kept.
questions.l5: Each installed construction product links to its declaration (and passport where available), its location in the building and its disassembly information, and the records are exportable.
questions.text: Does the agent keep construction-product records for the building (the declaration of performance and conformity under Regulation (EU) 2024/3110 Art. 13, and the construction digital product passport once delegated acts set it up under Arts. 75-79), together with disassembly information per ISO 20887?

questions.l1: No asset-level physical climate-risk assessment.
questions.l3: Hazards are assessed for some assets or under one scenario, and the results are not tied to the disclosure.
questions.l5: Every asset has a dated hazard and vulnerability assessment under stated scenarios, and the results feed the IFRS S2 disclosure with their inputs retained.
questions.text: Does the agent assess physical climate risk for each asset and feed the results into the operator's IFRS S2 disclosure where IFRS S2 is applied?

questions.l1: Occupant data are collected without documented purposes or retention.
questions.l3: Purposes and retention are documented, but default settings collect more than needed or retention is not enforced in configuration.
questions.l5: Each data flow has a documented purpose, minimised fields, pseudonymisation or aggregation where possible, enforced retention, and a record that the defaults were reviewed.
questions.text: Does the agent apply data protection by design and by default to tenant and occupant data (occupancy sensing, access logs, energy use) per GDPR Art. 25 as interpreted in EDPB Guidelines 4/2019, collecting only what each stated purpose needs?

questions.l1: No ZEB gating.
questions.l3: One deadline is applied to all buildings, or ZEB evidence is incomplete.
questions.l5: Owner type and permit date determine the applicable date; each building has a ZEB evidence pack against the national Art. 11 threshold; buildings exempted under Art. 7(4) are logged with their permit date.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU EPBD Art. 7(1); EU EPBD Art. 11
questions.text: Does the agent gate zero-emission-building compliance for new buildings by owner type (new buildings owned by public bodies from 1 January 2028, all new buildings from 1 January 2030, EPBD Art. 7(1)) and evidence each building against the zero-emission-building definition in Art. 11 as transposed?

questions.l1: No building automation system, or one with no retained energy logs.
questions.l3: Energy use is logged and benchmarked, but loss detection, interoperability or indoor-environmental-quality monitoring is missing.
questions.l5: All Art. 13(10) capabilities are evidenced with retained logs, efficiency-loss alerts reach the responsible person, and each building's threshold status is recorded.
questions.text: For non-residential buildings above the EPBD thresholds (heating or air-conditioning output over 290 kW by 31 December 2024, over 70 kW by 31 December 2029, Art. 13(9)), does the building automation system the agent runs provide the Art. 13(10) capabilities: continuous monitoring, logging, analysis and adjustment of energy use; benchmarking and detection of efficiency losses; interoperability; and indoor-environmental-quality monitoring?

questions.l1: No path for owners, tenants or managers to access building-systems data.
questions.l3: Data are provided on request or by hand, or third-party sharing has no consent record.
questions.l5: Self-service machine-readable access, consent-based third-party sharing with a consent log, and no access charge to owners, tenants or managers.
questions.text: Does the agent give building owners, tenants and managers direct access to their building systems' data, and make those data available to a third party on their consent, without additional cost to them (EPBD Art. 16(1) and (3))?

questions.l1: Life-cycle GWP is not calculated.
questions.l3: GWP is calculated for some buildings, or not by the national Annex III method.
questions.l5: Each in-scope new building has a dated GWP calculation by the national Annex III method, disclosed in its certificate, with the inputs retained.
questions.text: Does the agent calculate the life-cycle global warming potential of new buildings per EPBD Annex III and record it for the energy performance certificate, from 1 January 2028 for new buildings over 1 000 m² and from 1 January 2030 for all new buildings (Art. 7(2))?

questions.l1: Parking and recharging provision are not tracked against Art. 14.
questions.l3: Recharging points are counted, but pre-cabling, ducting or bicycle-parking ratios are not checked.
questions.l5: Each in-scope building has a recorded count of spaces, recharging points, pre-cabled and ducted spaces and bicycle spaces checked against the national ratios, with gaps assigned to an owner.
questions.text: For new non-residential buildings, and those undergoing major renovation, with more than five car parking spaces, does the agent track the EPBD Art. 14(1) requirements as transposed: at least one recharging point per five spaces, pre-cabling for at least 50% of spaces with ducting for the rest, and bicycle parking of at least 15% of average or 10% of total user capacity?

questions.l1: Disclosed characteristics or objectives cannot be traced to asset-level data.
questions.l3: Asset-level data exist for most claims, but they are not reconciled to the published disclosure or not retained per reporting period.
questions.l5: Every disclosed characteristic or objective maps to asset-level data retained per reporting period and reconciled to the published disclosure, with differences explained and recorded.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU SFDR Art. 8; EU SFDR Art. 9
questions.text: Where the operator manages a financial product that promotes environmental characteristics (SFDR Art. 8) or has sustainable investment as its objective (Art. 9) through real estate, does the agent keep the asset-level data behind each disclosed characteristic or objective, reconciled to the published disclosure?

questions.l1: Adaptation-alignment claims are made without reference to the Annex II criteria.
questions.l3: Claims cite the Annex II activity, but evidence is missing for some of its criteria.
questions.l5: Each claim names the Annex II activity and criteria applied, links evidence for every criterion, and is re-tested when the asset or the criteria change.
questions.text: Where the operator claims taxonomy alignment for climate change adaptation, does the agent test each claim against the technical screening criteria in Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2139 Annex II for the activity concerned and keep the evidence?

ubiquity-to-utility.certificationPath: L1 Basic energy monitoring → L2 Grid-connected with NERC CIP compliance → L3 ISO 50001 certified energy management → L4 Predictive grid optimization with renewable integration → L5 Autonomous energy ecosystem governance with verified decarbonization
ubiquity-to-utility.description: Sustainable energy generation to consumption — covering the full energy value chain from renewable generation through grid management, storage, distribution, and end-use optimization with emphasis on grid reliability, decarbonization, and energy equity.
ubiquity-to-utility.euAIActClassification: Annex III §2 — safety components in the management and operation of the supply of gas, heating or electricity
keyRisks: Grid instability from AI-managed renewable intermittency
Cyberattack on AI-controlled grid infrastructure (NERC CIP violation)
Energy poverty exacerbation through algorithmic pricing optimization
Carbon credit fraud in AI-managed offset programs
Cascading blackout from autonomous load-shedding decisions
ubiquity-to-utility.name: Ubiquity to Utility

questions.l1: Agent hosts, tools and integrations are not considered in CIP-002 categorisation
questions.l3: Agent hosts are categorised, but tools and integrations added later are not re-assessed
questions.l5: Every agent component touching BES operations is in the categorisation inventory with its impact rating, additions trigger re-categorisation before use, and the inventory is reconciled with deployment records each review cycle
questions.text: Does the entity's BES Cyber System categorisation under NERC CIP-002 (current effective version) include every host, tool and integration the agent uses to read or act on BES operations?

questions.l1: No renewable integration optimization; energy dispatch does not prioritize renewable sources or manage intermittency
questions.l3: Dispatch maximises renewable share, but grid-stability constraints are checked only after dispatch changes and curtailment reasons are not recorded
questions.l5: Dispatch decisions record renewable share, forecast inputs and curtailment reasons; grid-stability constraints are checked before each dispatch change; renewable share is reported against the target with the calculation method documented
questions.text: Does the agent's dispatch optimisation track the renewable share it achieves against the renewable energy target of Directive (EU) 2018/2001 Art. 3 as amended by Directive (EU) 2023/2413, while checking grid-stability constraints before each dispatch change?

questions.l1: No systematic energy performance monitoring; energy consumption data is collected but not analyzed against baselines or targets
questions.l3: EnPIs are tracked against baselines and significant energy uses identified per Clause 6.3, but deviations are not investigated or linked to action plans
questions.l5: The energy review is updated on each significant change, EnPIs are tracked against documented baselines with normalisation variables, significant energy uses have action plans with verified results, and deviations are investigated and recorded
questions.text: Does the agent manage energy performance monitoring per ISO 50001:2018 Clause 6.3 energy review and Clause 6.4 energy performance indicators (EnPIs)?

questions.l1: No GO records; renewable electricity claims are not backed by cancelled Guarantees of Origin
questions.l3: Agent tracks Guarantees of Origin and manages certificate portfolios, but does not prevent double-counting or automate disclosure reporting
questions.l5: Every renewable claim the agent produces is matched by ID and period to cancelled GOs, a double-counting check runs before each disclosure, and the disclosure report traces each claim to its GO records
questions.text: Does the agent manage Guarantees of Origin for the renewable electricity claims it produces — issue, transfer and cancellation records, cancellation before a claim is disclosed, and no double counting — per Directive (EU) 2018/2001 Art. 19 as amended by Directive (EU) 2023/2413?

questions.l1: The agent can change load or setpoints with no operator-approved envelope
questions.l3: Recommendations stay within operator-approved setpoints, but out-of-envelope actions are not technically blocked or logged with authorisation state
questions.l5: Every automated action is logged with the operator authorisation state, actions outside the pre-approved envelope require human confirmation, and the operator stop is tested to reach a safe state
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 14(4)(d)-(e) where the agent is an Annex III point 2 safety component
questions.text: Are the agent's load-adjustment recommendations and actions bounded by operator-approved setpoints, with any intervention outside the pre-approved envelope requiring human confirmation and an operator stop that brings the system to a safe state?

questions.l1: No energy equity assessment; pricing and distribution algorithms do not consider vulnerable consumer impact
questions.l3: Agent identifies energy-poor households using defined indicators and flags pricing decisions that may increase energy poverty, but does not proactively optimize for equitable access
questions.l5: Comprehensive energy equity integration with vulnerable consumer identification, affordability impact modeling for all pricing decisions, targeted efficiency program recommendations, and transparent reporting on energy poverty metrics per Art. 24
questions.text: Does the agent assess energy equity and affordability impact per EU Energy Efficiency Directive 2023/1791 Article 24 energy poverty provisions?

questions.l1: No Article 6 compliance; carbon credit transactions do not track corresponding adjustments or prevent double-counting
questions.l3: Agent tracks carbon credit provenance and flags potential double-counting risks, but corresponding adjustment calculations are manual
questions.l5: Full Article 6 compliance with automated corresponding adjustment calculations, ITMO tracking, share of proceeds management for Art. 6.4, environmental integrity verification, and transparent registry integration
questions.text: Does the agent support Paris Agreement Article 6 corresponding adjustments for international carbon credit transfers with double-counting prevention?

questions.l1: No storage-specific safety monitoring; battery energy storage systems are not monitored for thermal runaway or degradation risks
questions.l3: Basic storage parameters (state of charge, temperature, cycle count) are monitored with threshold alerts, but cell-level data, safety-system test records and degradation reporting are missing
questions.l5: Cell-level temperature, voltage and state-of-health are monitored against documented thresholds, safety-system tests are recorded on schedule, threshold breaches trigger the documented response, and degradation trends are reported
questions.regulatoryRef: IEC 62933-5-2 — Safety requirements for grid-connected EES systems
questions.text: Does the agent maintain energy storage system safety and performance monitoring per IEC 62933-5-2 safety requirements for grid-connected energy storage?

questions.l1: The agent can change IBR settings or firmware with no ride-through check
questions.l3: Changes are gated by human approval, but the ride-through settings check is manual and not linked to the change record
questions.l5: Every IBR change has a recorded pre-change check against the PRC-029-1 ride-through settings with result and approver, and a change that would alter ride-through capability is held for engineering review
questions.text: When the agent proposes or makes a control-setting or firmware change on an inverter-based resource, does it check the change against the resource's NERC PRC-029-1 ride-through settings before the change is applied?

questions.l1: No ports/services baselines exist; services are enabled ad-hoc and unauthorized exposure is not detected
questions.l3: Maintains a baseline for most BES Cyber Systems and alerts on some deviations, but approvals/justifications and evidence retention are incomplete
questions.l5: Continuous CIP-007-6 R1 compliance with automated baselining, change approvals with documented business need, authenticated service inventories, drift detection, and audit-ready evidence bundles per BES Cyber System
questions.text: Does the agent enforce NERC CIP-007-6 R1 Ports and Services controls by maintaining baselines of enabled logical ports/services on each BES Cyber System, approving and documenting required services, and detecting/alerting on unauthorized enablement?

questions.l1: No OT RBAC model; control actions and configuration changes are not governed by standardized roles/rights
questions.l3: Defines roles and limits some actions, but role engineering is incomplete and authorization decisions are inconsistently enforced across OT interfaces
questions.l5: IEC 62351-8-aligned RBAC with formal role engineering, least-privilege rights mapping to IEC 61850/SCADA control points, strong authentication binding, break-glass governance, and complete authorization/audit evidence
questions.text: Does the agent implement role-based access control for power system operations per IEC 62351-8 (role definition, role assignment, access rights mapping, and authorization enforcement for control actions)?

questions.l1: No IEC 61850 interoperability; substation integration relies on proprietary mappings or manual operations
questions.l3: Supports partial IEC 61850 data models and messaging, but configurations and change control are manual and security constraints are inconsistently applied
questions.l5: Full IEC 61850 interoperability with validated SCL workflows, deterministic control messaging support, protection/control coordination safeguards, and standardized integration testing for substation automation
questions.text: Does the agent support secure interoperability with substation automation systems per IEC 61850 (including data modeling, MMS/GOOSE/Sampled Values messaging constraints, and configuration management via SCL) for grid monitoring and control use cases?

questions.l1: No permitting workflow support; permit documentation and timelines are unmanaged
questions.l3: Tracks key permit milestones and documents, but does not provide end-to-end timeline compliance monitoring or multi-authority coordination
questions.l5: Every permit dossier is generated from project data with the applicable statutory deadlines tracked, authority interactions are logged through the contact point, grid-connection dependencies are linked, and the dossier history is exportable
questions.text: Does the agent manage renewable project permit-granting workflows per Directive (EU) 2018/2001 Art. 16-16f as amended by Directive (EU) 2023/2413, including documentation, statutory deadline tracking and single-contact-point coordination?

questions.l1: Agent model, tool and software vendors are outside the CIP-013 plan
questions.l3: Agent vendors are in the plan, but software integrity and authenticity of model or tool updates is not verified
questions.l5: Every agent model, tool and software update has recorded integrity and authenticity verification, and vendor notifications and remote-access controls are evidenced under R2
questions.text: Does the entity's NERC CIP-013-2 supply chain cyber security risk management plan cover the agent's model, tool and software vendors — vendor incident notification and coordination, vulnerability disclosure, software integrity and authenticity verification, and vendor remote access (R1.2.1-R1.2.6) — with implementation evidence (R2)?

questions.l1: No determination whether the agent is a safety component; no logs or override/stop design
questions.l3: Classification documented; logs kept and named human overseers assigned, but override and stop are untested
questions.l5: Classification recorded with its reasoning, Art. 12 logs retained and protected from alteration, override and stop exercised in drills with results recorded, and the evidence pack dated against the 2 Dec 2027 application date
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Annex III point 2, Art. 12, Art. 14(4)(d)-(e)
questions.text: Where the agent is a safety component in the supply of gas, heating or electricity (AI Act Annex III point 2), does it keep automatic event logs over its lifetime (Art. 12) and give operators the ability to override its output and stop it to a safe state (Art. 14(4)(d)-(e)), ready for the 2 Dec 2027 application date?

questions.l1: Agent traffic is not baselined and is invisible to internal network security monitoring
questions.l3: Agent traffic is in the network data feeds and baselined, but anomalies involving the agent are evaluated ad hoc
questions.l5: Agent action logs are correlated with INSM detections, evaluations and escalations are recorded, and retention and protection of INSM data are evidenced per R2-R3
questions.text: Is the agent's network activity inside high impact and medium impact (with External Routable Connectivity) BES Cyber System ESPs covered by the entity's internal network security monitoring per NERC CIP-015-1 — fed to detection (R1), with anomaly data retained until action is complete (R2) and protected from unauthorised deletion or modification (R3)?

questions.l1: IBR changes do not trigger model re-verification
questions.l3: Model re-verification is triggered manually after some changes, and results are not linked to the change record
questions.l5: Every IBR change opens a model re-verification record with result and date, linked to the change record, and the evidence is exported to the planning entities
questions.text: After a control-setting or firmware change on an inverter-based resource, does the agent trigger re-verification of the resource's model under the entity's NERC MOD-026-2 model verification process and keep the evidence for the planning entities?
